\section{CS1. The adèlic source and its compact unit
projection}\label{cs1.-the-aduxe8lic-source-and-its-compact-unit-projection}

Write \[
\mathbb A_{\mathbb Q}=\mathbb R\times\mathbb A_f,\qquad
\widehat{\mathbb Z}=\prod_p\mathbb Z_p,\qquad
K=\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\times}.
\tag{CS1.1}
\] Use Lebesgue measure at the real place and finite additive Haar
measure with \(\operatorname{vol}(\widehat{\mathbb Z})=1\). The adèlic
Bruhat--Schwartz space is the locally convex inductive limit of the
spaces of finite sums \(f_i(v)\phi_i(x_f)\), where
\(f_i\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R)\) and the \(\phi_i\) belong to one
finite-dimensional space of locally constant, compactly supported
functions on \(\mathbb A_f\). On each such stage the topology is a
finite direct sum of the ordinary real Schwartz topology.

Put \[
\mathcal S(\mathbb A_{\mathbb Q})_0
=\left\{F:F(0)=0,\ \int_{\mathbb A_{\mathbb Q}}F(x)\,dx=0\right\},
\quad
\mathcal R=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}
\{F-F(q\,\cdot):F\in\mathcal S(\mathbb A_{\mathbb Q}),\
q\in\mathbb Q^\times\},
\] \[
D=\mathcal S(\mathbb A_{\mathbb Q})_0/\overline{\mathcal R}.
\tag{CS1.2}
\] The closure is taken in \(\mathcal S(\mathbb A_{\mathbb Q})_0\) with
its subspace topology. Rational scaling preserves both endpoint
functionals, since \(|q|_{\mathbb A}=1\), so every displayed difference
belongs to that moment-null space even when its generating \(F\) does
not. This is the full-difference reading of the source's ``subspace of
\(\mathcal S(\mathbb A_{\mathbb Q})_0\) generated by the differences.''
The source line does not separately write a domain after its \(f\); the
distinction and its mathematically forced consequence are recorded in
CS2A.

The group \(K\) acts on finite coordinates. Its normalized Haar average
\(P_K\) is continuous on this source: each test function is fixed by an
open subgroup of \(K\), so its average is a finite average on that
test-function stage. The average commutes with rational scaling and
preserves both endpoint conditions. It consequently descends to a
continuous idempotent on \(D\).

Every idèle class has a unique representative \((u,k)\), with \(u>0\)
and \(k\in K\). To see this, multiply its finite component by the
positive rational with opposite finite valuations, and then use the sign
in \(\mathbb Q^\times\) to make its real component positive. Uniqueness
follows because a rational number with every finite valuation zero is
\(\pm1\), and positivity excludes the minus sign. Thus \[
C_{\mathbb Q}=\mathbb A_{\mathbb Q}^{\times}/\mathbb Q^\times
\ \cong\ \mathbb R_{>0}^{\times}\times K,\qquad |(u,k)|=u.
\tag{CS1.3}
\] This is a coordinate on the authors' already constructed idèle-class
group.

\section{CS2. An exact topological identification of the source
sector}\label{cs2.-an-exact-topological-identification-of-the-source-sector}

Define \[
\mathcal S_0^{\mathrm{even}}
=\left\{f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R):
f(-v)=f(v),\quad f(0)=0,\quad\int_{\mathbb R}f(v)\,dv=0\right\},
\] \[
j:\mathcal S_0^{\mathrm{even}}\longrightarrow D,\qquad
j(f)=[f\otimes1_{\widehat{\mathbb Z}}].
\tag{CS2.1}
\] This is continuous, and its image is fixed by \(K\).

We construct its continuous inverse on \(P_KD\). A \(K\)-invariant
finite Schwartz function is a finite linear combination of \[
1_{d\widehat{\mathbb Z}},\qquad d\in\mathbb Q_{>0}.
\tag{CS2.2}
\] Here \(d\widehat{\mathbb Z}\) is the product of the balls
\(p^{v_p(d)}\mathbb Z_p\). To prove the claim, choose the finitely many
primes on which the function is nonstandard. At each such prime, compact
support bounds valuations below and local constancy makes the function
constant on one sufficiently small ball around zero. Unit invariance
leaves a finite list of valuation shells and that final ball. Each shell
is the difference of two nested ball indicators. Taking tensor products
gives (CS2.2).

These ball indicators are linearly independent. In one local factor,
evaluation successively on the shells of largest and then smaller
absolute values proves independence of a finite list of nested balls.
Finite tensor products of independent lists are independent, and every
proposed relation involves such a finite product. This also proves that
the following definition is independent of its expansion.

For \(f^{\mathrm{ev}}(v)=(f(v)+f(-v))/2\), define on \(K\)-averaged
finite sums \[
B\bigl(f\otimes1_{d\widehat{\mathbb Z}}\bigr)(v)
=f^{\mathrm{ev}}(dv),
\qquad
B(F):=B(P_KF)
\quad\text{on the full source.}
\tag{CS2.3}
\] On each finite stage this is a finite sum of fixed real dilations and
the even projection, hence is continuous into
\(\mathcal S^{\mathrm{even}}(\mathbb R)\). The defining inductive-limit
topology proves continuity on the full source.

The endpoint identities are exact: \[
B(F)(0)=F(0),\qquad
\int_{\mathbb R}B(F)(v)\,dv
=\int_{\mathbb A_{\mathbb Q}}F(x)\,dx.
\tag{CS2.4}
\] For a ball tensor the second identity follows from \[
\operatorname{vol}(d\widehat{\mathbb Z})
=\prod_p p^{-v_p(d)}=d^{-1},
\qquad
\int_{\mathbb R}f^{\mathrm{ev}}(dv)\,dv
=d^{-1}\int_{\mathbb R}f(v)\,dv.
\tag{CS2.5}
\] The first identity is immediate; averaging does not change either
endpoint functional. Thus \(B\) maps the source in (CS1.2) into
\(\mathcal S_0^{\mathrm{even}}\).

For \(q\in\mathbb Q^\times\), direct substitution on a ball tensor gives
\[
B\bigl((f\otimes1_{d\widehat{\mathbb Z}})(q\,\cdot)\bigr)(v)
=f^{\mathrm{ev}}(dv)
=B(f\otimes1_{d\widehat{\mathbb Z}})(v).
\tag{CS2.6}
\] Indeed the new finite ball is \((d/|q|)\widehat{\mathbb Z}\), while
the new even real function is \(f^{\mathrm{ev}}(|q|v)\). Since \(P_K\)
commutes with this scaling, (CS2.6) holds on the full source. Continuity
makes \(B\) vanish on \(\overline{\mathcal R}\), so it descends to a
continuous map \(\bar B:D\to\mathcal S_0^{\mathrm{even}}\).

The two compositions are \[
\bar B\,j=\mathrm{id},\qquad j\,\bar B=P_K\quad\text{on }D.
\tag{CS2.7}
\] For the second identity, individual tensors need not themselves be
moment-null, so first work with differences before taking a quotient
class. Put \(G=f\otimes1_{d\widehat{\mathbb Z}}\) and
\(H_d=G(d\,\cdot)=f(dv)\otimes1_{\widehat{\mathbb Z}}\). Let
\(\widetilde j\) denote tensoring with \(1_{\widehat{\mathbb Z}}\) on
all even Schwartz functions. The exact identity is \[
G-\widetilde j(BG)
=(G-G(d\,\cdot))+\tfrac12(H_d-H_d(-\,\cdot))
\ \in\mathcal R.
\tag{CS2.7a}
\] Both parenthesized differences have zero endpoint moments, whether or
not their generating functions do. Sum (CS2.7a) over a radial-ball
expansion of \(P_KF\), with \(F\) moment-null. Only then take its class
in \(D\). This proves \(j\bar B[F]=P_K[F]\), with every class taken on
its actual domain.

Finally \(P_KD=D^K\). One inclusion follows from averaging. For a fixed
quotient class, choose a representative \(F\). Its \(K\)-orbit lies in a
finite averaging orbit modulo an open subgroup. Averaging its equal
quotient classes therefore gives the same class. We have proved the
actual topological isomorphism \[
\boxed{j:\mathcal S_0^{\mathrm{even}}\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ D^K,
\qquad j^{-1}=\bar B|_{D^K}.}
\tag{CS2.8}
\] In particular, this identification neither discards the closed
coinvariant relation nor assumes it has no kernel.

\section{CS2A. Why the generating domain must be
retained}\label{cs2a.-why-the-generating-domain-must-be-retained}

Let \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{null}}\) denote instead the span of
\(F-F(q\,\cdot)\) with \(F\) itself moment-null. Then
\(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{null}}\subset\mathcal R\), and there is a natural
continuous surjection \[
D_{\mathrm{null}}:=
\mathcal S(\mathbb A_{\mathbb Q})_0/
\overline{\mathcal R_{\mathrm{null}}}
\longrightarrow D.
\tag{CS2A.1}
\] This alternative quotient is genuinely larger. Here is a direct proof
which also identifies the source of the difference.

For a prime \(p\), expand a \(K\)-averaged Schwartz function as
\(\sum_d f_d\otimes1_{d\widehat{\mathbb Z}}\), and define the
two-component continuous functional \[
\ell_p(F)=\sum_d v_p(d)
\left(f_d(0),\ d^{-1}\int_{\mathbb R}f_d(v)\,dv\right),
\qquad \ell_p(F):=\ell_p(P_KF)
\text{ before averaging.}
\tag{CS2A.2}
\] The sum is finite, its expansion is unique by CS2, and continuity
follows on each finite test-function stage. Put
\(\epsilon(F)=(F(0),\int_{\mathbb A}F)\). On ball tensors, scaling
changes the index \(d\) to \(d/|q|\) and leaves the two displayed
endpoint values unchanged. Hence \[
\ell_p(F(q\,\cdot))
=\ell_p(F)-v_p(|q|)\epsilon(F).
\tag{CS2A.3}
\] It follows that \(\ell_p\) vanishes on
\(\overline{\mathcal R_{\mathrm{null}}}\), but not on all of
\(\mathcal R\). Indeed, take any even Schwartz \(f\) and \[
G=f\otimes1_{\widehat{\mathbb Z}}
-(f\otimes1_{\widehat{\mathbb Z}})(p\,\cdot).
\] Then \(G\) is moment-null, its summation is zero by rational
reindexing, and \[
\ell_p(G)=\left(f(0),\int_{\mathbb R}f\right).
\tag{CS2A.4}
\] The endpoint map on even Schwartz functions is onto \(\mathbb C^2\):
for example the functions \(e^{-\pi v^2}\) and \(v^2e^{-\pi v^2}\) have
endpoint pairs \((1,1)\) and \((0,1/(2\pi))\). Thus these are nonzero
classes in the alternative quotient whenever that pair is nonzero.

In particular, the injective summation and Fourier-graph claim in the
original source cannot hold on \(D_{\mathrm{null}}\) with this topology:
(CS2A.4) supplies an explicit kernel. The full-difference reading in CS1
removes exactly these displayed differences, and CS2--CS3 prove the
needed sector result for it. Even under the alternative reading, the map
(CS2A.1) and the commuting summation maps give the same summation image
and the same Hausdorff first-cohomology receiver. Its degree-zero kernel
contains additional classes, so its \(H^0\) must not be described by
(CS5.3).

The complete difference between the two quotient spaces can also be
computed. Give \[
V=\bigoplus_{p\ {\rm prime}}\mathbb C^2
\tag{CS2A.5}
\] the locally convex direct-sum topology, and put
\(\mathscr L(F)=(\ell_p(F))_p\). A fixed test-function stage has only
finitely many relevant primes in its radial-ball expansion. Thus
\(\mathscr L\) has finite support on every test function and is
continuous into \(V\).

Choose the continuous endpoint section
\(\sigma:\mathbb C^2\to\mathcal S(\mathbb A_{\mathbb Q})\) given by
tensoring \[
\sigma(a,b)_\infty(v)
=a(1-2\pi v^2)e^{-\pi v^2}
+b\,2\pi v^2e^{-\pi v^2}
\tag{CS2A.6}
\] with \(1_{\widehat{\mathbb Z}}\). The Gaussian moments give
\(\epsilon(\sigma(a,b))=(a,b)\). Define the continuous finite-sum map \[
\mathscr T(v)=\sum_p
\bigl(\sigma(v_p)-\sigma(v_p)(p\,\cdot)\bigr)
\in\mathcal R,\qquad
\mathscr L\mathscr T=\mathrm{id}_V.
\tag{CS2A.7}
\] The second identity is (CS2A.3) at every prime.

Write \(r_q(F)=F-F(q\,\cdot)\). Modulo \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{null}}\),
this depends only on \(\epsilon(F)\), because subtracting
\(\sigma(\epsilon F)\) makes its argument moment-null. Also \[
r_{qr}(F)\equiv r_q(F)+r_r(F)
\pmod{\mathcal R_{\mathrm{null}}}.
\tag{CS2A.8}
\] Indeed their difference is a rational difference with generating
function \(F(q\,\cdot)-F\), which is moment-null. The sign \(q=-1\)
contributes zero in this quotient, since
\(r_{-1}(F)=\tfrac12r_{-1}(F-F(-\,\cdot))\). Unique factorization,
including negative prime exponents, now gives \[
r_q(F)\equiv
\sum_p v_p(|q|)\,r_p(\sigma(\epsilon F))
=\mathscr T\mathscr L(r_q(F))
\pmod{\mathcal R_{\mathrm{null}}}.
\tag{CS2A.9}
\] Thus \((I-\mathscr T\mathscr L)\mathcal R\subset
\mathcal R_{\mathrm{null}}\). Continuity gives the same inclusion for
closures. It follows that the exact quotient map has the topological
splitting \[
\boxed{
D_{\mathrm{null}}\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ D\oplus V,\qquad
[F]_{\mathrm{null}}\longmapsto([F],\mathscr L F).
}
\tag{CS2A.10}
\] For injectivity, if \(F\in\overline{\mathcal R}\) and
\(\mathscr LF=0\), the closure inclusion puts \(F\) in
\(\overline{\mathcal R_{\mathrm{null}}}\). For surjectivity, start with
any representative \(F\) of the required \(D\)-class and replace it by
\(F+\mathscr T(v-\mathscr LF)\). A continuous inverse sends \(([F],v)\)
to \([F-\mathscr T\mathscr LF+\mathscr T v]_{\mathrm{null}}\).
Independence of the representative and continuity follow from the
closure inclusion and the defining quotient topology. This proves the
full alternative receiver and its connecting maps; the additional
summand records two endpoint directions at every prime.

\section{CS3. The overlap, Fourier transform, and all rational
summands}\label{cs3.-the-overlap-fourier-transform-and-all-rational-summands}

On the trivial \(K\)-sector, the source overlap space
\(\bigcap_{\beta\in\mathbb R}\mu^\beta\mathcal S(C_{\mathbb Q})\) is the
Fréchet space \[
H=\left\{h\in C^\infty(\mathbb R_{>0}):
p_{N,j}(h):=\sup_{u>0}(u^N+u^{-N})
|(u\partial_u)^jh(u)|<\infty\quad(N,j\ge0)\right\}.
\tag{CS3.1}
\] To verify both the set and topology, use \(x=\log u\). The ordinary
multiplicative Schwartz seminorms are the polynomially weighted
derivative seminorms in \(x\); the source additionally requires every
factor \(e^{\beta x}\). Derivatives of \(e^{\beta x}h(e^x)\) are finite
sums of \(e^{\beta x}\partial_x^\ell h(e^x)\). Polynomial factors in
\(x\) are bounded by a constant times \(e^{|x|}\), and
\(e^{N|x|}\le e^{Nx}+e^{-Nx}\le2e^{N|x|}\). These identities bound every
source seminorm by finitely many (CS3.1) seminorms and conversely.
Integer \(N\) suffice for every real \(\beta\).

For \(f\in\mathcal S_0^{\mathrm{even}}\), summation of its actual adèlic
representative at \((u,1)\) gives \[
S f(u):=\Sigma(jf)(u)
=\sum_{q\in\mathbb Q^\times}f(qu)1_{\widehat{\mathbb Z}}(q)
=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}}f(nu)
=2\sum_{n\ge1}f(nu).
\tag{CS3.2}
\] The criterion in the middle step is
\(q\in\widehat{\mathbb Z}\cap\mathbb Q=\mathbb Z\). Both rational signs
are present, and the final factor two is retained.

Use the real Fourier convention \[
\widehat f(t)=\int_{\mathbb R}f(v)e^{-2\pi ivt}\,dv.
\tag{CS3.3}
\] Choose the corresponding character of
\(\mathbb A_{\mathbb Q}/\mathbb Q\) and self-dual measures; at finite
places the annihilator of \(\widehat{\mathbb Z}\) is itself, with volume
one. Direct Fourier integration of its indicator is therefore the same
indicator. Consequently the adèlic Fourier transform of
\(f\otimes1_{\widehat{\mathbb Z}}\) is
\(\widehat f\otimes1_{\widehat{\mathbb Z}}\). Fourier transformation
preserves both vanishing endpoint conditions and evenness, and
\(\widehat{\widehat f}=f\) on this even space.

Set \[
(Rh)(u)=u^{-1}h(1/u),\qquad R^2=\mathrm{id}.
\tag{CS3.4}
\] For an arbitrary even real Schwartz function, Poisson summation
retains the exact endpoint identity \[
S f(u)-u^{-1}S\widehat f(1/u)
=u^{-1}\int_{\mathbb R}f(v)\,dv-f(0).
\tag{CS3.5}
\] Indeed the full lattice sums have their zero summands \(f(0)\) and
\(u^{-1}\widehat f(0)\), and \(\widehat f(0)=\int f\). For our actual
moment-null source both terms on the right vanish, so \[
S\widehat f=R S f,\qquad
R S\widehat f=S f.
\tag{CS3.6}
\] This is the exact plus/minus gluing identity, including the factor
\(u^{-1}\).

The map \(S:\mathcal S_0^{\mathrm{even}}\to H\) is continuous. At
\(u\ge1\), each logarithmic derivative of the series is bounded by a
sufficiently high Schwartz seminorm times a convergent sum
\(\sum_{n\ge1}n^{-M}\), \(M>1\). For \(u\le1\), (CS3.6) expresses the
answer through the Fourier transform at \(1/u\ge1\), multiplied by
\(u^{-1}\). Fourier continuity and one additional endpoint weight prove
the required bounds. The same arguments justify termwise
differentiation.

It is also injective. For \(\Re s>1\), absolute convergence and the
substitution \(v=nu\) give \[
\int_0^\infty S f(u)u^s\,\frac{du}{u}
=2\zeta(s)\int_0^\infty f(v)v^s\,\frac{dv}{v}.
\tag{CS3.7}
\] If \(Sf=0\), choose any real \(c>1\). Since \(\zeta(c+it)\ne0\) on
this half-plane, the Mellin transform of \(f|_{\mathbb R_{>0}}\)
vanishes on the line \(c+it\). It is the Fourier transform of the
integrable function \(x\mapsto e^{cx}f(e^x)\), with Fourier frequency
sign fixed by \(e^{itx}\). Fourier injectivity gives \(f(e^x)=0\);
evenness gives \(f=0\) on \(\mathbb R\). This proves the source-sector
injectivity independently of the full adèlic coinvariant theorem.

\section{CS4. The actual three-point
sheaf}\label{cs4.-the-actual-three-point-sheaf}

Let \[
X=\{0,\eta,\infty\},\qquad
U_+=\{0,\eta\},\quad U_-=\{\eta,\infty\},\quad
U=\{\eta\}.
\tag{CS4.1}
\] The nonempty opens are \(U,U_+,U_-,X\). The point \(\eta\) is
generic; \(0,\infty\) are closed. These are the authors' base labels.

For each chart retain its two separate endpoint lines, \[
E_+=\mathbb C e_{+,0}\oplus\mathbb C e_{+,1},\qquad
E_-=\mathbb C e_{-,0}\oplus\mathbb C e_{-,1},
\quad
A_\pm=\mathcal S_0^{\mathrm{even}}\oplus E_\pm.
\tag{CS4.2}
\] The index 0 labels the value-at-zero endpoint functional, and index 1
labels the integral endpoint functional. These are the two explicit
summands in the source definition of \(\mathcal S(M)\), separately on
each chart.

Define \[
\mathscr F(U_+)=A_+,\quad
\mathscr F(U_-)=A_-,\quad
\mathscr F(U)=H,
\] \[
r_+(f,e_+)=S f,\qquad
r_-(h,e_-)=R S h=S\widehat h.
\tag{CS4.3}
\] Every endpoint restriction is zero, exactly as in restmaps. Define \[
\mathscr F(X)=\{(a,b)\in A_+\oplus A_-:r_+a=r_-b\},
\qquad \mathscr F(\varnothing)=0.
\tag{CS4.4}
\] Use the evident restrictions from \(X\). The only nontrivial sheaf
gluing condition is the cover \(X=U_+\cup U_-\), and it is precisely
(CS4.4). A cover of \(U_+\) must contain \(U_+\), since no smaller open
contains 0; the same holds for \(U_-\) and \(\infty\). The overlap is a
singleton. Thus these formulas construct a genuine sheaf, including its
topology on every section space.

Under \(j\) on the two source coordinates and (CS1.3) on the overlap,
this is the \(P_K\)-image sheaf of the actual Connes--Consani sheaf.
Averaging commutes with summation, restrictions, and Fourier transform,
and is the identity on the endpoint lines. It is therefore a sheaf
idempotent and gives a direct-summand sheaf. This precise use of
``trivial finite-unit sector'' does not silently identify fixed classes
in an arbitrary non-Hausdorff quotient with quotients of fixed
representatives.

\section{CS5. Ordinary cohomology, including every endpoint
line}\label{cs5.-ordinary-cohomology-including-every-endpoint-line}

Fix the ordered cover \((U_+,U_-)\). Its complex is \[
C^0=A_+\oplus A_-,\qquad C^1=H,\qquad
d(a,b)=r_+a-r_-b.
\tag{CS5.1}
\] This computes ordinary sheaf cohomology in the category of complex
vector-space sheaves, before taking closures. Here is an elementary
derived-functor verification. A sheaf on this space is exactly a diagram
\(D_+\to H\leftarrow D_-\). Global sections are the kernel of the
displayed difference. Short exact sequences of diagrams give short exact
sequences of these two-term complexes and their cohomology long exact
sequences. The degree-one functor is effaceable: embed the diagram into
one with chart spaces \(D_+\oplus H,D_-\oplus H\), overlap \(H\), and
restriction maps the projections to \(H\); embed \(a\) as \((a,r_+a)\),
\(b\) as \((b,r_-b)\), and act identically on \(H\). The new difference
map is onto \(H\), so its degree-one cohomology vanishes. Thus this
effaceable cohomology functor is the right-derived global-section
functor. There are no higher terms, and \[
H^i(X,\mathscr F)=0\quad(i\ge2).
\tag{CS5.2}
\]

By (CS3.6) and injectivity of \(S\), \(d((f,e_+),(h,e_-))=0\) if and
only if \(f=\widehat h\), equivalently \(h=\widehat f\). Consequently \[
\boxed{
H^0(X,\mathscr F)
=\{((f,e_+),(\widehat f,e_-)):
f\in\mathcal S_0^{\mathrm{even}},\ e_+\in E_+,\ e_-\in E_-\}.
}
\tag{CS5.3}
\] This is a topological isomorphism from
\(\mathcal S_0^{\mathrm{even}}\oplus E_+\oplus E_-\) onto the kernel,
because Fourier transformation and the coordinate projections are
continuous. There are four independent endpoint lines, rather than two
endpoint lines identified across the charts.

Write \[
J=S(\mathcal S_0^{\mathrm{even}})\subset H.
\tag{CS5.4}
\] The minus restriction has the same image \(J\), since Fourier
transformation is a bijection of the source. Moreover
\(d((f,0),(0,0))=Sf\). Therefore \[
\operatorname{im}d=J,\qquad
\boxed{H^1_{\mathrm{alg}}(X,\mathscr F)=H/J.}
\tag{CS5.5}
\] The subscript emphasizes that the ordinary cokernel has not been
replaced by a closed-image quotient. Give it the quotient locally convex
topology. Its closure of zero is \(\overline J/J\), and its maximal
Hausdorff quotient is \[
H^1_{\mathrm{Haus}}(X,\mathscr F):=
H/\overline J,\qquad
0\longrightarrow\overline J/J
\longrightarrow H/J
\longrightarrow H/\overline J
\longrightarrow0.
\tag{CS5.6}
\] This sequence is algebraically exact without an additional image
theorem. CS11 subsequently proves \(J=\overline J\), so its left term is
zero for this particular source.

\section{CS6. The exact comparison with the existing source
image}\label{cs6.-the-exact-comparison-with-the-existing-source-image}

The earlier real source map, with its original factors, is \[
\mathcal E f(u)=u^{1/2}\sum_{n\ge1}f(nu),
\qquad
\mathcal C=\overline{\mathcal E(\mathcal S_0^{\mathrm{even}})}^{\mathcal A},
\tag{CS6.1}
\] where \(\mathcal A\) has exactly the weighted derivative seminorms
(CS3.1). Although \(H\) and \(\mathcal A\) have the same underlying
class of functions, their receiving formulas differ. Define the
comparison explicitly: \[
U:H\longrightarrow\mathcal A,\qquad
(Uh)(u)=\tfrac12 u^{1/2}h(u),
\qquad
(U^{-1}k)(u)=2u^{-1/2}k(u).
\tag{CS6.2}
\] For \(D_u=u\partial_u\), \[
D_u^j(u^a h)
=u^a\sum_{\ell=0}^j\binom j\ell a^{j-\ell}D_u^\ell h.
\tag{CS6.3}
\] Since \((u^N+u^{-N})u^{\pm1/2}
\le2(u^{N+1}+u^{-(N+1)})\), these give the concrete continuity estimates
\[
p_{N,j}(Uh)
\le\sum_{\ell=0}^j\binom j\ell
(1/2)^{j-\ell}p_{N+1,\ell}(h),
\] \[
p_{N,j}(U^{-1}k)
\le4\sum_{\ell=0}^j\binom j\ell
(1/2)^{j-\ell}p_{N+1,\ell}(k).
\tag{CS6.4}
\] Both compositions in (CS6.2) are the identity, so this is a
topological isomorphism. Formula (CS3.2) now gives, without removing its
original scalar or power, \[
S f=2u^{-1/2}\mathcal E f,\qquad
USf=\mathcal E f.
\tag{CS6.5}
\] Topological isomorphisms commute with closure. It follows that \[
\boxed{
\overline J^{\,H}=U^{-1}\mathcal C
=\{2u^{-1/2}k(u):k\in\mathcal C\}.
}
\tag{CS6.6}
\] Thus the requested source-image comparison includes both topologies
and both inverses, rather than only a formal equality of summation
expressions.

\section{CS7. Raw Mellin transform, original zeta, and the Hausdorff
quotient}\label{cs7.-raw-mellin-transform-original-zeta-and-the-hausdorff-quotient}

Retain the two Mellin maps separately: \[
\mathcal M_0h(s)=\int_0^\infty h(u)u^s\,\frac{du}{u},
\qquad
\mathcal Mk(s)=\int_0^\infty k(u)u^{s-1/2}\,\frac{du}{u}.
\tag{CS7.1}
\] They satisfy \[
\mathcal M_0h=2\mathcal M(Uh),\qquad
\Theta:=\mathcal M U=\tfrac12\mathcal M_0.
\tag{CS7.2}
\] The previous theorem S1 proves \(\mathcal M:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B\)
is a topological isomorphism, where \[
\mathcal B=\left\{F\text{ entire}:
b_{A,M}(F):=\sup_{|\Re s|\le A}
(1+|\Im s|)^M|F(s)|<\infty\ \text{for every }A,M\ge0\right\}.
\tag{CS7.3}
\] Consequently \(\Theta\) is a topological isomorphism. For example its
full inverse, on the real line \(c=1/2\), is \[
(\Theta^{-1}F)(u)
=\frac{u^{-1/2}}{\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}
F(1/2+it)u^{-it}\,dt.
\tag{CS7.4}
\] This is \(2u^{-1/2}\) times S1's inverse with coefficient
\(1/(2\pi)\); both factors remain explicit.

Equation (CS3.7) is the raw arithmetic identity \[
\mathcal M_0Sf(s)=
2\zeta(s)\int_0^\infty f(v)v^s\,\frac{dv}{v},
\qquad
\Theta Sf(s)=
\zeta(s)\int_0^\infty f(v)v^s\,\frac{dv}{v}
\quad(\Re s>1).
\tag{CS7.5}
\] For the retained source \[
f_0(v)=\frac{\pi}{2}v^2(2\pi v^2-3)e^{-\pi v^2},
\tag{CS7.6}
\] S2's exact calculation gives \[
\Theta Sf_0(s)=F_0(s)
=\frac{s(s-1)}8\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s),
\qquad
\mathcal M_0Sf_0(s)=2F_0(s)
=\frac{s(s-1)}4\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s).
\tag{CS7.7}
\] The entire continuation and exceptional values are \[
F_0(0)=F_0(1)=\frac18,\qquad
\mathcal M_0Sf_0(0)=\mathcal M_0Sf_0(1)=\frac14,
\tag{CS7.8}
\] \[
F_0(-2r)
=\frac{r(2r+1)(-1)^r\pi^r}{2\,r!}\zeta'(-2r)
=\frac{(1+2r)(2r)}8\pi^{-(1+2r)/2}
\Gamma((1+2r)/2)\zeta(1+2r)\ne0
\quad(r\ge1).
\tag{CS7.9}
\] The raw Mellin value at every such point is \(2F_0(-2r)\). This
retains the endpoint contributions and the Gamma-pole/trivial-zero
cancellation. It does not make the completed product a replacement for
the original zeta function.

For additional endpoint precision, let
\(a_f(s)=\int_0^\infty f(v)v^s\,dv/v\). Its meromorphic continuation has
possible simple poles at \(-2r\), \(r\ge1\), with residues
\(f^{(2r)}(0)/(2r)!\), obtained by subtracting the real Taylor
polynomial on \(0<v<1\). At the original trivial zeros, \[
\mathcal M_0Sf(-2r)
=2\zeta'(-2r)\frac{f^{(2r)}(0)}{(2r)!}.
\tag{CS7.10}
\] At the two endpoints, \(a_f(1)=\tfrac12\int_{\mathbb R}f=0\), the
zeta residue at 1 is one, and \(\zeta(0)=-1/2\), so \[
\mathcal M_0Sf(1)=2a_f'(1),\qquad
\mathcal M_0Sf(0)=-a_f(0).
\tag{CS7.11}
\] Thus the source's two zero moment conditions do not erase these
receiver values.

Let \(\mathscr Z\) be the set of distinct actual nontrivial zeros of the
original \(\zeta\), with their full multiplicities \(m_\rho\), and let
\[
\mathcal I=
\{F\in\mathcal B:F^{(j)}(\rho)=0\
\text{for every }\rho\in\mathscr Z,\ 0\le j<m_\rho\},
\qquad \mathcal Q=\mathcal B/\mathcal I.
\tag{CS7.12}
\] S5 proves \(\mathcal M\mathcal C=\mathcal I\) on these exact spaces.
Combining this established theorem with (CS6.6) proves \[
\boxed{
\overline J=\Theta^{-1}\mathcal I,\qquad
H^1_{\mathrm{Haus}}(X,\mathscr F)
\xrightarrow[\ \ [h]\mapsto[\tfrac12\mathcal M_0h]\ \ ]{\ \sim\ }
\mathcal Q.
}
\tag{CS7.13}
\] The map and its inverse are continuous quotient maps induced by the
homeomorphism \(\Theta\), because it takes exactly one closed subspace
to the other. On ordinary cohomology it is the surjection \[
H^1_{\mathrm{alg}}(X,\mathscr F)=H/J
\longrightarrow\mathcal Q,\qquad
\ker=\overline J/J.
\tag{CS7.14}
\] This proves the Hausdorff identification without presupposing
equality with ordinary cohomology. CS11 supplies that equality by
constructing the actual inverse source function. Every original-zero jet
and its full order is retained by (CS7.12).

\section{CS8. Unshifted scaling, all endpoint characters, and the Čech
sign}\label{cs8.-unshifted-scaling-all-endpoint-characters-and-the-ux10dech-sign}

For \(a>0\), the source actions on the main chart coordinates and the
overlap are \[
\rho_+(a)f(v)=f(v/a),\qquad
\rho_-(a)h(v)=a\,h(av),\qquad
\rho_H(a)g(u)=g(u/a).
\tag{CS8.1}
\] They preserve the moment-null even Schwartz space and are continuous.
On the four endpoint lines their exact characters are \[
\begin{array}{c|cccc}
\text{line}&e_{+,0}&e_{+,1}&e_{-,0}&e_{-,1}\\ \hline
\text{multiplier}&1&a&a&1.
\end{array}
\tag{CS8.2}
\] These follow respectively by evaluation at zero and change of
variables in the real integral. In particular the minus chart uses the
source's extra scalar \(a\); it does not have the same ordered endpoint
characters as the plus chart.

Direct substitution proves \[
r_\pm\rho_\pm(a)=\rho_H(a)r_\pm,\qquad
\widehat{\rho_+(a)f}=\rho_-(a)\widehat f.
\tag{CS8.3}
\] Thus the Fourier graph and all four endpoint lines carry the actual
source action. Under (CS6.2)--(CS7.2), \[
U\rho_H(a)U^{-1}k(u)=a^{1/2}k(u/a),\qquad
\Theta\rho_H(a)\Theta^{-1}F(s)=a^sF(s).
\tag{CS8.4}
\] The infinitesimal operator on raw \(H\) is \(-u\partial_u\); on
\(\mathcal A\) it is \(1/2-u\partial_u\); on \(\mathcal B\) it is
multiplication by the original variable \(s\). No operator has been
silently shifted. On the quotient the arithmetic operator is exactly \[
T_a[F]=[a^sF(s)],
\quad
T_n=n^L=\sqrt n\,V_n^{\mathrm{centered}},
\tag{CS8.5}
\] where the superscript distinguishes the earlier centered dilation
from an integral transfer generator.

The source Weyl lift exchanges chart sections by the identity and acts
on overlap sections by \(R\). On the ordered Čech complex (CS5.1), its
actual cochain action is \[
W^0(a,b)=(b,a),\qquad W^1g=-Rg.
\tag{CS8.6}
\] Indeed \[
dW^0(a,b)=r_+b-r_-a
=-R(r_+a-r_-b)=-Rd(a,b).
\tag{CS8.7}
\] The extra minus sign is the orientation sign from reversing the
ordered chart pair. Both degrees square to the identity.

On \(H^0\), the main Fourier-graph coordinate transforms as
\(f\mapsto\widehat f\), and the endpoint lines are exchanged by their
chart labels. On the Hausdorff \(H^1\) quotient, changing variables
\(v=1/u\) gives \[
\mathcal M_0(Rg)(s)=\mathcal M_0g(1-s),\qquad
\boxed{W^1[F(s)]=[-F(1-s)].}
\tag{CS8.8}
\] The ideal is preserved either by the source identity \(RJ=J\) and
closure, or by the original functional equation with its multiplicities.
The source's unshifted compatibility remains \[
\rho_H(a)R=aR\rho_H(a^{-1}),
\qquad
T_aW^1=aW^1T_{a^{-1}}.
\tag{CS8.9}
\] This proves the spectral reflection and its chain sign without
assuming critical-line location or positivity.

\section{CS9. The single-closed-point support
maps}\label{cs9.-the-single-closed-point-support-maps}

For the closed subset \(\{0\}\), the ordinary support functor is
\(\ker(r_+:A_+\to H)\). Its derived complex is \[
L_0=[A_+\xrightarrow{\,r_+\,}H].
\tag{CS9.1}
\] For \(\{\infty\}\) use \[
L_\infty=[A_-\xrightarrow{\,r_-\,}H].
\tag{CS9.2}
\] These derived identifications follow by the same short-exact-complex
and effacement proof as CS5 for the single arrow. Source injectivity and
(CS3.6) yield \[
H^0_{\{0\}}(X,\mathscr F)=E_+,\qquad
H^0_{\{\infty\}}(X,\mathscr F)=E_-,
\] \[
H^1_{\{0\}}(X,\mathscr F)=H/J,\qquad
H^1_{\{\infty\}}(X,\mathscr F)=H/J,
\qquad H^i_{\{0\}}=H^i_{\{\infty\}}=0\quad(i\ge2).
\tag{CS9.3}
\] The two support-to-global chain maps, with positive restriction
differentials in both local presentations, are \[
L_0\longrightarrow C^\bullet:
\quad a\longmapsto(a,0),\quad g\longmapsto g,
\] \[
L_\infty\longrightarrow C^\bullet:
\quad b\longmapsto(0,b),\quad g\longmapsto-g.
\tag{CS9.4}
\] Their chain identities follow from \(d(a,0)=r_+a\) and
\(d(0,b)=-r_-b\). Hence both induce first-cohomology isomorphisms, with
respectively \(+\mathrm{id}\) and \(-\mathrm{id}\) in the displayed
quotient coordinates.

For completeness, the restriction \(H^0(X,\mathscr F)\to A_-\) is onto:
given \((h,e_-)\), choose the global section with plus coordinate
\(\widehat h\), arbitrary plus endpoints, and minus coordinate \(h\).
Its kernel is \(E_+\). This proves directly that the connecting map
\(A_-\to H^1_{\{0\}}\) is zero and gives the exact sequence \[
0\longrightarrow E_+
\longrightarrow H^0(X,\mathscr F)
\longrightarrow A_-
\xrightarrow{\,0\,}H/J
\xrightarrow{\,\mathrm{id}\,}H/J
\longrightarrow0.
\tag{CS9.5}
\] The analogous sequence for the other closed point has the
support-to-global sign from (CS9.4). Passing the individual
first-cohomology spaces to their Hausdorff quotients gives the same
isomorphisms with \(\mathcal Q\), with exactly those signs. This does
not assert that replacing every term of an arbitrary ordinary
localization sequence by its Hausdorff quotient preserves exactness.

The Weyl map from \(L_0\) to \(L_\infty\) is the identity on chart
coordinates and \(+R\) on degree one, because \(r_-=Rr_+\). Together
with (CS9.4), this gives precisely the global \(-R\) in (CS8.6),
reconciling the local and global sign conventions.

\section{CS10. Result and limits of this
comparison}\label{cs10.-result-and-limits-of-this-comparison}

The constructed object is the explicit
\(K=\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{\times}\) summand of the original
Connes--Consani sheaf. Its source chart coordinate is topologically
\(\mathcal S_0^{\mathrm{even}}(\mathbb R)\), as proved by the two
inverse maps in (CS2.7). Its overlap restriction is the full rational
sum \(2\sum_{n\ge1}f(nu)\). Its ordinary \(H^0\) is the Fourier graph
with four separate endpoint lines, and its ordinary \(H^1\) is \(H/J\).
The exact topological comparison is \[
\begin{array}{ccc}
H &\xrightarrow{\ U:h\mapsto\frac12u^{1/2}h\ }&\mathcal A\\
\big\downarrow{\mathrm{quotient}}&&\big\downarrow{\mathrm{quotient}}\\
H/\overline J&\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }&\mathcal A/\mathcal C
\xrightarrow[\mathcal M]{\ \sim\ }\mathcal B/\mathcal I=\mathcal Q.
\end{array}
\tag{CS10.1}
\] Every map in this diagram has been specified on its actual topology,
and the ordinary-to-Hausdorff kernel is \(\overline J/J\). The
comparison carries unshifted idèle scaling to multiplication by \(a^s\),
and the ordered Čech Weyl action to \(-F(1-s)\).

This proves an actual source-sheaf realization and its exact connection
to all original-zeta zero jets. It does not prove a finite-field
Frobenius structure, positivity of the original Weil form, separation of
the weights of a new lifting obstruction, or RH. Such a conclusion is
not one of the hypotheses used in any map or quotient above.

\section{CS11. The actual image is closed, with its complete
inverse}\label{cs11.-the-actual-image-is-closed-with-its-complete-inverse}

The later complete derivation SSI0--SSI9 in
\nolinkurl{EXACT_SCHWARTZ_SUMMATION_IMAGE.md}, independently checked in
ESI0--ESI9 of \nolinkurl{EXACT_SCHWARTZ_IMAGE_INDEPENDENT_CHECK.md},
strengthens the source-image statement used above. Both full proofs are
retained in this edition. It gives \[
\mathcal M_0S:\mathcal S_0^{\mathrm{even}}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal I
\tag{CS11.1}
\] as a topological isomorphism. For \(b\in H\) with
\(F=\mathcal M_0b\in\mathcal I\), its exact inverse is \[
f_F(x)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}
\frac{F(2+it)}{2\zeta(2+it)}x^{-2-it}\,dt\quad(x>0),
\qquad Sf_F=b.
\tag{CS11.2}
\] It extends to an even Schwartz function on the whole real line, with
\[
f_F(0)=0,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}f_F=0,\qquad
\frac{f_F^{(2r)}(0)}{(2r)!}=\frac{F(-2r)}{2\zeta'(-2r)}
\quad(r\ge1).
\tag{CS11.3}
\] The derivation cancels the nontrivial-zero poles with all their
actual multiplicities, retains the simple trivial-zero poles of
\(F/(2\zeta)\), proves rapid bounds on every pole-cleared vertical
strip, and shifts the inverse Mellin contour with every residue
retained. SSI4 proves continuous bounds from the two vertical boundary
lines; SSI5--SSI6 prove all source derivatives and endpoint moments.
Thus the inverse is a map into the actual source topology, not merely a
limiting representative in a quotient.

Since \(\mathcal I\) is closed and \(\mathcal M_0\) is a homeomorphism,
(CS11.1) gives \[
J=\overline J=\mathcal M_0^{-1}\mathcal I=\Theta^{-1}\mathcal I,
\qquad \overline J/J=0.
\tag{CS11.4}
\] The last equality of inverse images uses the exact scalar relation
\(\Theta=\tfrac12\mathcal M_0\) and the fact that \(\mathcal I\) is a
complex vector subspace. Consequently (CS7.13) identifies the ordinary
first cohomology itself with \(\mathcal Q\), using exactly its displayed
map \([b]\mapsto[\tfrac12\mathcal M_0b]\). The four independent endpoint
lines, both support-to-global signs, the Weyl action, all actual zero
jets and the unshifted arithmetic action remain as calculated in CS5 and
CS8--CS9.

This theorem kills precisely the comparison kernel \(\overline J/J\). It
does not kill the prime-indexed endpoint summand of CS2A: that summand
occurs in a different quotient of the source and is already in the
summation kernel before taking its image. The two quotients and their
topologies have not been identified. Neither vanishing is presented as
Deligne's weight-separated lifting obstruction.

\begin{center}\rule{0.5\linewidth}{0.5pt}\end{center}

\chapter{Supported localization, Fourier lifts, and exact weight maps
---
CSL0--CSL10}\label{supported-localization-fourier-lifts-and-exact-weight-maps-csl0csl10}

Proof source: \nolinkurl{CC_SUPPORTED_LOCALIZATION_AND_WEIGHT_MAPS.md}.

\chapter{The supported localization maps of the original-zeta
sheaf}\label{the-supported-localization-maps-of-the-original-zeta-sheaf}

Complete derivation, 24 September 2026. Proof locators CSL0--CSL10.

\section{CSL0. Construction stage and
sources}\label{csl0.-construction-stage-and-sources}

The supporting datum is \(\tau\langle Z_1;\text{no }Z_2\rangle\). Its
comparison with the unique generic point uses the complete chart
reconstruction CG1--CG3, after the complete arithmetic has been
recovered. All vector spaces, sums, scalar factors and quotient
operations in this note occur in the coefficient sheaf over that
support. None is an arithmetic operation on \(\tau\), a metric on it, or
a definition of the earlier counting process. The two chart summation
maps remain separately labelled.

The corrected argument and relevant verbatim passages were recalled
before this calculation; PC04 in the private prerequisite ledger records
that reading. In particular, the retracted addition at \(\tau\) is not
used, and fixed support is not substituted for trivial action on its
stalk.

The original author source is Alain Connes and Caterina Consani,
\emph{Schemes over \(\mathbb F_1\) and zeta functions},
\href{https://arxiv.org/abs/0903.2024v3}{arXiv:0903.2024v3}, §5. Its
unchanged author file is
\nolinkurl{sources/CC_0903_2024_v3/author_source/announc3.tex}. Root
read lines1376--1667 in full, including the sheaf, both restriction
maps, the Fourier proof and the localization sequence. The source
archive is retained unchanged. The spectral comparison below uses the
complete construction in
\nolinkurl{CC_SHEAF_ORIGINAL_ZETA_COHOMOLOGY.md} and S1--S7 in
\texttt{GLOBAL\_MELLIN\_SYNTHESIS.md}; the former proves the exact
finite-unit sector of the adelic sheaf and the latter its closed
summation image. These are named derivations, not original-author
claims.

The weight comparison is with Pierre Deligne, \emph{La conjecture de
Weil. II},
\href{https://www.numdam.org/item/PMIHES_1980__52__137_0/}{§3.6}, as
reconstructed in DC1--DC8 of
\nolinkurl{DELIGNE_INVARIANT_CYCLE_QUOTIENT.md}. The present calculation
gives the actual supported-cohomology maps of the CC coefficient sheaf.
It does not replace Deligne's inertia and geometric duality terms with
similarly named analytic spaces.

\section{CSL1. Exact sheaf and unshifted
actions}\label{csl1.-exact-sheaf-and-unshifted-actions}

Let \(X=\{x_+,\eta,x_-\}\), with opens \[
\varnothing,\quad U=\{\eta\},\quad
U_+=\{x_+,\eta\},\quad U_-=\{x_-,\eta\},\quad X.
\tag{CSL1.1}
\] The notation \(x_+,x_-\) distinguishes the two closed chart points
from the integer zero and from \(\tau\). In the author's notation these
are \(0,\infty\); that is a chart notation, not an equation identifying
\(\tau\) with zero.

There is an exact topological comparison with the later signed CC
construction: send its points \((+,\eta,-)\) to \((x_+,\eta,x_-)\). The
open sets of CC.tex lines499--505 are exactly (CSL1.1), so this map and
its inverse are continuous. The underlying map of the full involution
exchanges the two closed points and fixes the generic point. Therefore
this homeomorphism intertwines the underlying involutions, and pullback
transports the coefficient sheaf below to that space, with its stalks
and all cohomology unchanged. The original signed stalk formulas remain
\(\alpha^*T=\epsilon T^{-1}\) and \(\alpha^*J=\epsilon J\), with
\(J^2=\epsilon\). The topological pullback is not asserted to be a
comparison of the two structure sheaves or an action of those full
signed stalk generators on the new coefficient sheaf. Its domain is
precisely the underlying topological space, which is sufficient for the
sheaf and support calculations being made here.

Let \(S\) be the even real Schwartz space with complex coefficients and
with both moments zero: \[
S=\{f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R):f(-v)=f(v),\ f(0)=0,\ \int_{\mathbb R}f(v)\,dv=0\}.
\tag{CSL1.2}
\] Set \(V_+=S\oplus\mathbb C^2\), \(V_-=S\oplus\mathbb C^2\). Denote
the additional coordinates by \((c_0,c_1)\), retaining the value and
integral labels. The overlap is \[
A=\{a\in C^\infty(\mathbb R_{>0}):
\sup_{u>0}(u^N+u^{-N})|(u\partial_u)^j a(u)|<\infty
\text{ for every }N,j\ge0\}.
\tag{CSL1.3}
\] The exact comparison with S1's centred source is the topological
isomorphism \[
\mathcal T:\mathcal A\longrightarrow A,\qquad
(\mathcal T k)(u)=2u^{-1/2}k(u),\qquad
\mathcal T^{-1}a(u)=\tfrac12u^{1/2}a(u).
\tag{CSL1.4}
\] Multiplication by either displayed power shifts each seminorm by at
most one integer weight; Leibniz's formula gives a finite sum of
derivative seminorms. Thus both maps are continuous and preserve exactly
the stated spaces.

Define \[
\Sigma f(u)=2\sum_{n\ge1}f(nu),\qquad
Ra(u)=u^{-1}a(u^{-1}),\qquad
r_+(f,c_0,c_1)=\Sigma f,\quad r_-(h,d_0,d_1)=R\Sigma h.
\tag{CSL1.5}
\] These are the original CC restriction maps in the finite-unit sector.
The factor2 comes from both signs in \(\mathbb Q^\times\); it is not
discarded. Poisson summation gives, for general even Schwartz \(h\), \[
\Sigma\widehat h(u)
=u^{-1}\Sigma h(u^{-1})+u^{-1}h(0)-\int_{\mathbb R}h(v)\,dv.
\tag{CSL1.6}
\] Here \(\widehat h(t)=\int h(v)e^{-2\pi ivt}\,dv\). Therefore on \(S\)
\[
R^2=1,\qquad \widehat{\widehat h}=h,\qquad
R\Sigma h=\Sigma\widehat h.
\tag{CSL1.7}
\] The two omitted terms in the restricted identity are zero by the two
specified moment conditions; their formula and their independent
endpoint coordinates are retained. The convergence and continuity of
\(\Sigma:S\to A\) follow by Schwartz summation at infinity and (CSL1.6)
at zero, with logarithmic derivatives. Its injectivity also has an
elementary proof: for \(\Re s>1\), \[
\int_0^\infty\Sigma f(u)u^s\frac{du}{u}
=2\zeta(s)\int_0^\infty f(v)v^s\frac{dv}{v}.
\tag{CSL1.8}
\] If \(\Sigma f=0\), the nonvanishing Euler product on this half-plane
makes the second Mellin transform zero there. Fourier uniqueness on any
vertical line in that half-plane gives \(f=0\) on the positive axis, and
evenness gives \(f=0\) on \(\mathbb R\).

For \(a>0\), retain the unshifted actions \[
\begin{aligned}
T_a b(u)&=b(u/a),\\
\rho_+(a)(f,c_0,c_1)&=(f(\cdot/a),c_0,ac_1),\\
\rho_-(a)(h,d_0,d_1)&=(a h(a\cdot),ad_0,d_1).
\end{aligned}
\tag{CSL1.9}
\] Direct substitution shows \(r_\pm\rho_\pm(a)=T_a r_\pm\) and \[
T_aR=aRT_{a^{-1}},\qquad
\widehat{a h(a\cdot)}(v)=\widehat h(v/a).
\tag{CSL1.10}
\] Thus these are actions on the specified sheaf. No \(a^{-1/2}\)
character has been used to replace them.

\section{CSL2. The whole Cech complex and its
topology}\label{csl2.-the-whole-cech-complex-and-its-topology}

Each of \(U_+,U_-,U\) has a point whose only neighbourhood in that open
is the whole open. Sections there are the corresponding stalk functor,
hence exact. These opens are acyclic for every sheaf of vector spaces.
The Cech complex for this two-open cover therefore computes ordinary
sheaf cohomology: \[
D^0=V_+\oplus V_-,\qquad D^1=A,\qquad
d(v_+,v_-)=r_+v_+-r_-v_-.
\tag{CSL2.1}
\] This sign convention is fixed below. Let \[
J=\Sigma(S),\qquad C=\overline J^{\,A},\qquad
Q_{\rm alg}=A/J,\qquad Q_H=A/C,\qquad N=C/J.
\tag{CSL2.2}
\] By (CSL1.7), \(r_+(V_+)=r_-(V_-)=J\), so the sum of the chart images
is exactly \(J\), without a doubling of its arithmetic spectrum. Hence
\[
H^1(X,\Omega)=Q_{\rm alg},\qquad H^j(X,\Omega)=0\ (j\ge2),
\quad 0\longrightarrow N\longrightarrow Q_{\rm alg}
\longrightarrow Q_H\longrightarrow0.
\tag{CSL2.3}
\] The last arrow is precisely Hausdorffization for the quotient locally
convex topology. The construction of this sequence does not presuppose
\(J=C\). CSL10 now proves that equality by applying the complete
inverse-source theorem.

Injectivity of \(\Sigma\) and (CSL1.7) give the full zeroth cohomology:
\[
H^0(X,\Omega)=
\{((\widehat h,c_0,c_1),(h,d_0,d_1)):
h\in S,\ c_0,c_1,d_0,d_1\in\mathbb C\}.
\tag{CSL2.4}
\] In particular, all four labelled endpoint lines remain in the kernel.
The restriction to \(U\) has image \(J\), and its kernel consists
exactly of these four lines.

\section{CSL3. One closed support and an actual lifting
map}\label{csl3.-one-closed-support-and-an-actual-lifting-map}

Let \(Y_+=\{x_+\}\). Its complement is \(U_-\). The complex with support
on \(Y_+\) is represented by \[
K_+=[V_+\xrightarrow{r_+}A]
\quad\text{in degrees }0,1.
\tag{CSL3.1}
\] To prove this, use the localization cone of the chain map
\(D\to V_-[0]\), \((v_+,v_-)\mapsto v_-\). Its degree0 is
\(V_+\oplus V_-\), its degree1 is \(A\oplus V_-\), and its differential
is \((v_+,v_-)\mapsto(r_+v_+-r_-v_-,v_-)\). Changing degree1 coordinates
to \((b+r_-v_-,v_-)\) splits it as (CSL3.1) plus the contractible
identity complex on \(V_-\). This explicitly proves the claimed
quasi-isomorphism.

Consequently \[
H^0_{Y_+}(X,\Omega)=\mathbb C\oplus\mathbb C[1],\qquad
H^1_{Y_+}(X,\Omega)=Q_{\rm alg},\qquad H^j_{Y_+}=0\ (j\ge2),
\tag{CSL3.2}
\] where \(\mathbb C[1]\) means the character \(a\mapsto a\), not a
cohomological shift. The map \(K_+\to D\) is \(v\mapsto(v,0)\) in
degree0 and the identity on \(A\) in degree1. It induces the identity \[
H^1_{Y_+}(X,\Omega)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^1(X,\Omega).
\tag{CSL3.3}
\]

The connecting map from \(H^0(U_-,\Omega)\) into this supported \(H^1\)
is zero. This is proved by the continuous equivariant lift \[
\ell_-:V_-\longrightarrow H^0(X,\Omega),\qquad
(h,d_0,d_1)\longmapsto
((\widehat h,0,0),(h,d_0,d_1)).
\tag{CSL3.4}
\] Its restriction to \(U_-\) is the identity. Equation (CSL1.10) proves
equivariance, and the Fourier transform is continuous in the Schwartz
topology. Thus the exact lifting is actually constructed, including the
endpoint data. Its mechanism is Poisson summation and Fourier transform;
it is not presented as a new proof of weight separation.

For \(Y_-=\{x_-\}\), the analogous supported complex is
\([V_-\xrightarrow{r_-}A]\). Under the fixed sign of (CSL2.1), its map
to \(D\) is \(v\mapsto(0,v)\) in degree0 and multiplication by \(-1\) in
degree1. Both support choices are thereby retained with their correct
sign.

\section{CSL4. Both closed supports and the diagonal/difference
sequence}\label{csl4.-both-closed-supports-and-the-diagonaldifference-sequence}

Put \(Y=\{x_+,x_-\}\), whose complement is the generic open \(U\). A
complex representing \(R\Gamma_Y(X,\Omega)\) is \[
K^0=V_+\oplus V_-,\quad K^1=A\oplus A,\quad
d_K(v_+,v_-)=(r_+v_+,r_-v_-).
\tag{CSL4.1}
\] Here is an explicit localization-cone proof. Represent the
restriction to \(U\) by the chain map \(D\to A[0]\) which is \(r_+\) on
the first summand of \(D^0\). Choosing \(r_-\) instead gives a homotopic
map: their difference is the differential (CSL2.1). The shifted cone has
differential \[
(v_+,v_-)\longmapsto
(r_+v_+-r_-v_-,\ r_+v_+)
\quad\text{in }A\oplus A.
\tag{CSL4.2}
\] The invertible degree1 change \((k,b)\mapsto(b,b-k)\), with inverse
\((b_+,b_-)\mapsto(b_+-b_-,b_+)\), gives (CSL4.1). Its map to \(D\) is
the identity in degree0 and \((b_+,b_-)\mapsto b_+-b_-\) in degree1. The
boundary from \(A\) into supported degree1 is \(b\mapsto(b,b)\).

It follows, with all maps specified, that the complete nonzero portion
of the localization sequence is \[
0\to\mathbb C^4\to H^0(X,\Omega)\xrightarrow{\Sigma\widehat{\phantom h}}A
\xrightarrow{\beta}Q_{\rm alg}\oplus Q_{\rm alg}
\xrightarrow{\pi}Q_{\rm alg}\to0,
\tag{CSL4.3}
\] where the middle map on the graph (CSL2.4) sends it to
\(\Sigma\widehat h\), and \[
\beta(b)=([b],[b]),\qquad \pi([b_+],[b_-])=[b_+-b_-].
\tag{CSL4.4}
\] Exactness can also be checked without derived notation. The kernel of
\(\beta\) is \(J\). If \([b_+]=[b_-]\), the pair is diagonal and in its
image. Every class is the image of \(([b],0)\), and all earlier kernels
have already been computed in (CSL2.4). This proves each arrow of
(CSL4.3).

After factoring out \(J\) in the middle, one obtains \[
0\longrightarrow Q_{\rm alg}\xrightarrow{q\mapsto(q,q)}
Q_{\rm alg}\oplus Q_{\rm alg}
\xrightarrow{(q_+,q_-)\mapsto q_+-q_-}Q_{\rm alg}
\longrightarrow0.
\tag{CSL4.5}
\] This row is split by \(q\mapsto(q,0)\). Hausdorffization here gives
exactly the same row with \(Q_H\) in all three places: this follows
directly from the explicit maps and the closed subspaces \(C\),
\(C\oplus C\), rather than from a general exactness claim about
Hausdorffization.

\section{CSL5. The mirror sign on cochains and its retained
action}\label{csl5.-the-mirror-sign-on-cochains-and-its-retained-action}

The mirror exchanges \(x_+,x_-\) and fixes \(\eta\), since the generic
point is unique. A carried exchanged \(Z_2\)-label at that fixed point
would have to equal its flip, which is impossible for either of its two
states. This derives the relevant absence of that label at
\(\tau\langle Z_1;\text{no }Z_2\rangle\). It does not make the stalk
involution the identity.

On the sheaf the mirror swaps the two chart sections and uses \(R\) on
the overlap. The induced map on the ordered Cech complex is \[
w_D^0(v_+,v_-)=(v_-,v_+),\qquad w_D^1(b)=-Rb.
\tag{CSL5.1}
\] Indeed, \(d(v_-,v_+)=\Sigma h-R\Sigma f=-R(\Sigma f-R\Sigma h)\). The
minus sign is the orientation sign from reversing the ordered cover;
omitting it would not give a chain map. This does not change the
author's assertion of spectral symmetry, but it fixes the actual action
under our displayed identification of \(H^1\).

On (CSL4.1) the induced map is \[
w_K^0(v_+,v_-)=(v_-,v_+),\qquad
w_K^1(b_+,b_-)=(Rb_-,Rb_+).
\tag{CSL5.2}
\] The identity \(Rr_-=r_+\), with the two chart labels exchanged,
verifies the chain-map identity. Consequently (CSL4.5) is equivariant
with mirror \(R\) on its first term, \((q_+,q_-)\mapsto(Rq_-,Rq_+)\) on
its middle term, and \(-R\) on its last term. Its continuous arithmetic-
and mirror-equivariant section is \[
s(q)=\tfrac12(q,-q).
\tag{CSL5.3}
\] The calculation is exact: \(\pi s(q)=q\), while
\(w_Ks(q)=\tfrac12(-Rq,Rq)=s(-Rq)\). The scalar \(1/2\) is in the
already constructed complex coefficient field. It has no interpretation
as halving \(\tau\).

\section{CSL6. Exact comparison with the original-zeta
receiver}\label{csl6.-exact-comparison-with-the-original-zeta-receiver}

Use the raw Mellin map \[
\mathcal M_0b(s)=\int_0^\infty b(u)u^s\frac{du}{u}.
\tag{CSL6.1}
\] From (CSL1.4) and S1, \[
\mathcal M_0\mathcal T=2\mathcal M,\qquad
\mathcal M_0T_a=a^s\mathcal M_0,\qquad
\mathcal M_0R b(s)=\mathcal M_0b(1-s).
\tag{CSL6.2}
\] All integrals converge absolutely in every fixed strip; the inverse
is \[
b(e^x)=\frac{e^{-cx}}{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}
(\mathcal M_0b)(c+it)e^{-itx}\,dt
\quad(c\in\mathbb R).
\tag{CSL6.3}
\] The estimates and contour shifts are those of S1 with the exact
change (CSL6.2). Thus \(\mathcal M_0\) is a topological isomorphism
\(A\to\mathcal B\).

Let \(\mathcal I\) be the closed ideal of full-order vanishing at every
original nontrivial zero, with its original multiplicity. S5 gives
\(\mathcal M_0 C=\mathcal I\), so \[
Q_H\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal Q=\mathcal B/\mathcal I,
\qquad[b]\longmapsto[\mathcal M_0b].
\tag{CSL6.4}
\] Under this exact isomorphism, the entire supported row (CSL4.5) is
the diagonal/difference row of the actual \(\mathcal Q\), with the same
full multiplicities and quotient topology. It is not an unrestricted
product of jets or an algebraic direct sum.

For the retained source function \[
f_0(v)=\frac\pi2v^2(2\pi v^2-3)e^{-\pi v^2},
\] the complete auxiliary transform is \[
\mathcal M_0\Sigma f_0(s)
=\frac{s(s-1)}4\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)=2F_0(s).
\tag{CSL6.5}
\] Its endpoint values are \(1/4\) at both0 and1. At each negative even
integer, with \(r\ge1\), its retained cancellation value is \[
(2F_0)(-2r)
=\frac{r(2r+1)(-1)^r\pi^r}{r!}\zeta'(-2r)
=\frac{(1+2r)(2r)}4\pi^{-(1+2r)/2}
\Gamma((1+2r)/2)\zeta(1+2r)\ne0.
\tag{CSL6.6}
\] These are values of the transform; the original \(\zeta\) still has
its pole at1 and trivial zeros at \(-2r\). Its unit and prime-power
repetitions remain in \[
\zeta(s)=1+\sum_{n\ge2}n^{-s}
=\prod_p(1-p^{-s})^{-1},\qquad
-\frac{\zeta'(s)}{\zeta(s)}
=\sum_p\sum_{m\ge1}(\log p)p^{-ms}
\quad(\Re s>1).
\tag{CSL6.7}
\] All these arithmetic labels belong to the recovered complete
arithmetic, not to the primitive support.

\section{CSL7. What the computed action says about
weights}\label{csl7.-what-the-computed-action-says-about-weights}

On an actual original-zero block at \(\rho\) of multiplicity \(m_\rho\),
multiplication by \(s\) is \(\rho I+N_\rho\), where
\(N_\rho^{m_\rho}=0\). Consequently the unshifted action in every
\(Q_H\) term above is \[
T_a=a^\rho\sum_{j=0}^{m_\rho-1}
\frac{(\log a)^j}{j!}N_\rho^j.
\tag{CSL7.1}
\] It follows from the original strip \(0<\Re\rho<1\), for \(a>1\), that
its character weight \(2\log_a|a^\rho|\) lies in \((0,2)\). The kernel,
middle terms and quotient of (CSL4.5) have these same character weights.
The diagonal and difference are explicit nonzero equivariant maps; they
are not forced to vanish by separated weights.

The endpoint kernel has the separately computed weights. In \(V_+\),
value has character1 and integral has character \(a\); in \(V_-\), value
has character \(a\) and integral has character1. Thus the four endpoint
lines have weights \(0,2,2,0\), in that order. This follows from
(CSL1.9), not from a weight assigned to a support point.

This weight computation states the exact analytic character action. It
does not assert that these spaces are finite-dimensional \(\ell\)-adic
cohomology, that their characters are algebraic Weil numbers, or that an
arithmetic weight filtration has been imported without a comparison.

\section{CSL8. The precise comparison with Deligne's localization
cross}\label{csl8.-the-precise-comparison-with-delignes-localization-cross}

In Deligne's theorem, the top obstruction group and the inertia term are
\[
O_i=H^{2N-i-1}(X_s,E)^\vee(-N),\qquad
K_i=H^{i-1}(X_{\bar\eta},E)_I(-1),
\tag{CSL8.1}
\] and the obstruction to specialization is \[
\operatorname{im}(\partial_i)/\partial_i j_i(K_i).
\tag{CSL8.2}
\] DC3--DC6 derives the Tate factors from tame inertia and the dualizing
complex of the smooth total space. Those operations give the weights
\(\le i\) on the classes and \(\ge i+1\) on the obstruction receiver.
They are additional geometric maps, not consequences of the name
``localization.''

For the CC sheaf calculated here, the exact specialization-like map
actually constructed by removing one closed point is (CSL3.3). It is an
isomorphism, with inverse the identity on the displayed quotient. The
restriction lift (CSL3.4) is explicit. For removal of both closed
points, the exact receiver and its maps are (CSL4.3)--(CSL4.5), and the
equivariant section is (CSL5.3). These are genuine applications of
localization to this coefficient sheaf, and every map has now been
calculated on its source.

In particular, neither supported calculation produces an uncomputed Tate
shift: the character identity (CSL7.1) determines its action. The
constructed comparison to the Mellin receiver is (CSL6.4), not an
identification with (CSL8.1). A geometric extension carrying an
additional normal direction can have a different dualizing or inertia
term; the preceding calculation makes no claim against such an
extension. Its exact current contribution is the original-zeta
cohomological receiver, its support maps, its Fourier lift, and its
mirror-equivariant split supported row. It does not certify completion
of the requested Deligne weight-lifting application.

\section{CSL9. All comparison arrows and retained
information}\label{csl9.-all-comparison-arrows-and-retained-information}

The following commuting formulas describe the full receiver used here:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal M_0\circ r_+&=2\,\mathcal M\circ\mathcal E,\\
\mathcal M_0\circ r_-&=2\,(F(s)\mapsto F(1-s))\circ\mathcal M\circ\mathcal E,\\
\overline{\mathcal M_0}^{\oplus2}\circ\beta
&=\operatorname{diag}\circ\overline{\mathcal M_0},\\
\overline{\mathcal M_0}\circ\pi
&=\operatorname{diff}\circ\overline{\mathcal M_0}^{\oplus2},\\
\overline{\mathcal M_0}^{\oplus2}\circ s(q)
&=\tfrac12(\overline{\mathcal M_0}q,-\overline{\mathcal M_0}q).
\end{aligned}
\tag{CSL9.1}
\] The first two formulas act on the Schwartz component and send each
explicitly retained endpoint summand to zero. The last three use the
quotient of \(\beta\) by its kernel \(J\), followed by the stated
Hausdorffization. Hence their domains and codomains are exactly the
displayed \(Q_H\) spaces. Every original-zero jet survives in
\(\mathcal Q\); CSL10 calculates the separately retained closure
difference as \(N=C/J=0\). The support remains
\(\tau\langle Z_1;\text{no }Z_2\rangle\), while the full coefficient
action, both charts and their orientation sign remain visible.

\section{CSL10. Exact image, strict maps, and the calculated comparison
kernel}\label{csl10.-exact-image-strict-maps-and-the-calculated-comparison-kernel}

The complete proof SSI0--SSI9 in
\nolinkurl{EXACT_SCHWARTZ_SUMMATION_IMAGE.md} constructs a continuous
inverse to \[
\mathcal M_0\Sigma:S\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal I.
\tag{CSL10.1}
\] Its independently checked proof ESI0--ESI9 is retained in
\nolinkurl{EXACT_SCHWARTZ_IMAGE_INDEPENDENT_CHECK.md}. With
\(F=\mathcal M_0b\), the inverse has the full formula \[
f_F(x)=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}
\frac{F(2+it)}{2\zeta(2+it)}x^{-2-it}\,dt\quad(x>0).
\tag{CSL10.2}
\] The pole-cleared strip estimate, contour residues and smooth even
extension in SSI4--SSI6 prove \(f_F\in S\), continuity in all Schwartz
seminorms, and \(\Sigma f_F=b\). Its even derivatives at zero are
exactly \((2r)!F(-2r)/(2\zeta'(-2r))\); both vanishing moments and every
nontrivial multiplicity are proved there. Thus the inverse does not
discard the trivial-zero data of the original function.

It follows, on the actual spaces already used in CSL2, that \[
J=\mathcal M_0^{-1}\mathcal I=C,\qquad N=0,
\qquad Q_{\mathrm{alg}}\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_H\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal Q.
\tag{CSL10.3}
\] Each map is a homeomorphism with the quotient topologies. Both chart
restrictions are strict onto \(J\): the plus chart has right inverse
\(b\mapsto(\Sigma^{-1}b,0,0)\), and the minus chart has right inverse
\(b\mapsto(\widehat{\Sigma^{-1}b},0,0)\). Poisson summation proves the
second identity. The Čech differential has right inverse from its image
\(b\mapsto((\Sigma^{-1}b,0,0),0)\), so its image is closed and its
ordinary first cohomology is already Hausdorff.

Therefore the one-point localization maps and the two-point
diagonal/difference row of CSL3--CSL5 are maps on the actual
original-zero quotient without any extra closure operation. Their signs,
common arithmetic action and section \(q\mapsto\tfrac12(q,-q)\) are
unchanged. This is the vanishing of the exact comparison kernel \(N\),
not a deduction that the source has pure weight or that the
independently calculated localization row is Deligne's cross.
