\section{GTR1. The actual sheaf and positive-degree
covers}\label{gtr1.-the-actual-sheaf-and-positive-degree-covers}

Use \(Y=\mathbb P^1(\mathbb C)\), \(D=\{0,\infty\}\),
\(Y^\circ=\mathbb C^\times\), and the CSP coefficient spaces \[
S=\{f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R;\mathbb C):f(-x)=f(x),\ f(0)=0,\ \int_{\mathbb R}f=0\},
\quad V_p=S\oplus E_p,\quad E_p=\mathbb C^2\quad(p=+,-),
\] \[
A=\{a\in C^\infty(\mathbb R_{>0}):
\sup_{u>0}(u^N+u^{-N})|(u\partial_u)^ja(u)|<\infty
\text{ for every }N,j\ge0\}.
\tag{GTR1.1}
\] The full restrictions are \[
\Sigma f(u)=2\sum_{k\ge1}f(ku),\quad
Ra(u)=u^{-1}a(u^{-1}),\quad
r_+(f,e)=\Sigma f,\quad r_-(h,e)=R\Sigma h.
\tag{GTR1.2}
\] Write \(J=\Sigma S\), \(Q=A/J\). The actual source-image theorem
proves closedness of \(J\) and the continuous inverse of
\(\Sigma:S\to J\). With \(i:D\hookrightarrow Y\), \[
\mathscr F=\underline A_Y\times_{i_*(A\oplus A)}i_*(V_+\oplus V_-).
\tag{GTR1.3}
\] On a connected open meeting one pole, a section consists of a
constant \(a\in A\) and \(v_p\in V_p\) with \(a=r_pv_p\); on an interior
connected open it is a constant \(a\). This follows directly from the
fibre product, and specifies the local maps used below.

For every recovered integer \(n\ge1\), let \(b_n(z)=z^n\), with both
poles fixed. The equality \(\pi b_n=\pi\) supplies the canonical
identification \(b_n^{-1}\mathscr F=\mathscr F\). This is an
identification of sheaves pulled from the same three-point diagram, not
an inverse geometric map.

The local multiplicities are \[
e_n(x)=\begin{cases}n,&x=0\text{ or }\infty,\\1,&x\in\mathbb C^\times,\end{cases}
\qquad \sum_{b_n(x)=y}e_n(x)=n.
\tag{GTR1.4}
\] At zero the local ring quotient is \(\mathbb C[z]_{(z)}/(z^n)\), of
length \(n\) with basis \(1,z,\ldots,z^{n-1}\); the coordinate \(w=1/z\)
gives the same calculation at infinity. Away from the poles the
derivative \(nz^{n-1}\) is nonzero, and there are exactly \(n\) distinct
roots. Thus (GTR1.4) includes both ramified points and every interior
sheet. It agrees with the flat quasi-finite weighting in the cited
source, without removing the ramification.

\section{GTR2. The weighted trace exists on the actual topological
sheaf}\label{gtr2.-the-weighted-trace-exists-on-the-actual-topological-sheaf}

Define \[
\operatorname{Tr}_n:b_{n*}b_n^{-1}\mathscr F=b_{n*}\mathscr F\longrightarrow\mathscr F
\tag{GTR2.1}
\] as follows. On a sufficiently small interior disk the inverse image
is a disjoint union of \(n\) disks, and the map on sections is \[
(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\longmapsto\sum_{j=1}^n a_j.
\tag{GTR2.2}
\] On a sufficiently small disk about a pole, the inverse image is one
pole disk and a section is \((r_pv_p,v_p)\). Its image is \[
(r_pv_p,v_p)\longmapsto(nr_pv_p,nv_p).
\tag{GTR2.3}
\] The restriction of (GTR2.3) to an interior subdisk equals (GTR2.2):
all \(n\) sheet values are the restriction \(r_pv_p\). Reordering the
sheets does not change the sum. These formulas therefore agree on a
basis of neighborhoods and every overlap, and define a sheaf morphism.
Each local map is a finite continuous linear operation on the specified
Fréchet spaces. At each pole both endpoint coordinates are multiplied by
\(n\); they are not discarded because their generic restriction
vanishes.

These local descriptions determine the map uniquely once its full
weighted stalk values are specified. Generic-sheet agreement alone would
not determine a map on the endpoint kernels \(E_p\). Formula (GTR2.3)
supplies that missing value explicitly from the local multiplicity.

The pullback unit \(u_n:\mathscr F\to b_{n*}b_n^{-1}\mathscr F\) is
diagonal on an interior disk and is the identity on a pole stalk. Hence
\[
\boxed{\operatorname{Tr}_n u_n=n\,1_{\mathscr F}.}
\tag{GTR2.4}
\] This is an equality on every stalk and therefore on sheaves. No
division by \(n\) is used in constructing the trace.

The finite proper map \(b_n\) has exact direct image on vector-space
sheaves. To see this without a finite-rank hypothesis, its direct-image
stalk at \(y\) is the finite direct sum of the stalks at
\(b_n^{-1}(y)\). Indeed small disjoint neighborhoods of the finite fibre
contain the inverse image of some neighborhood of \(y\): otherwise
properness supplies an accumulation point outside those neighborhoods
mapping to \(y\), a contradiction. Taking the corresponding neighborhood
limits proves the stalk formula. Finite direct sums and stalk functors
are exact. This also proves \(Rb_{n*}=b_{n*}\); derived global sections
of the pushforward equal those on the source. Thus (GTR2.1) gives an
actual transfer on all cohomology groups.

The formula is natural in every continuous morphism of coefficient
diagrams, since such maps commute with finite sums and multiplication by
\(n\). In particular it is natural for the actual sequence with overlap
coefficients \(J\to A\to Q\), retaining the entire \(J\). Composition is
exact: grouping roots in the composite cover multiplies their local
multiplicities, \[
e_{mn}(x)=e_n(x)e_m(b_n(x)),
\] and the two successive finite sums equal the single weighted sum.
Consequently the transfer for \(b_{mn}\) equals the composite transfer
for \(b_n\) and \(b_m\), with the direct-image identifications retained.

\section{GTR3. Transfer on the full cohomology and support
diagrams}\label{gtr3.-transfer-on-the-full-cohomology-and-support-diagrams}

Let \(P_n\) denote geometric pullback alone. The positive angular form
is \[
\vartheta=\frac{d\arg z}{2\pi},\qquad b_n^*\vartheta=n\vartheta.
\tag{GTR3.1}
\] The positive sphere form and its full integral are \[
\omega_Y=\frac{dx\wedge dy}{\pi(1+|z|^2)^2},\quad
\int_Yb_n^*\omega_Y
=2n^2\int_0^\infty\frac{r^{2n-1}}{(1+r^{2n})^2}\,dr=n.
\tag{GTR3.2}
\] CSP and CDW give the explicit global coefficient complex \[
D^0=V_+\oplus V_-\xrightarrow{r_+-r_-}D^1=A\xrightarrow0D^2=A.
\tag{GTR3.3}
\] Its groups are \(H^0=Z=\ker(r_+-r_-)\), \(H^1=Q\), \(H^2=A\). On this
model geometric pullback is \((1,1,n)\). In degree one it is the
identity because the original degree-zero overlap constants are
unchanged; in degree two (GTR3.2) gives the factor. These are invertible
operators on these already constructed complex coefficient groups.

Taking cohomology in (GTR2.4) and using the proved pullback values
determines the actual transfer: \[
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
&H^0(Y,\mathscr F)=Z&H^1(Y,\mathscr F)=Q&H^2(Y,\mathscr F)=A\\\hline
P_n&1&1&n\\
\operatorname{Tr}_n&n&n&1.
\end{array}
\tag{GTR3.4}
\] The map \((n,n,1)\) on (GTR3.3) is a continuous cochain
representative of these transfer values: its only nonzero differential
commutes with \(n\). No assertion that the map \(z\mapsto z^n\) has a
single-valued inverse is involved. This statement identifies the induced
cohomology maps and an explicit compatible coefficient representative;
it does not infer uniqueness of chain representatives from cohomology
alone.

At either pole the costalk groups are \(E_p,Q,A\) in degrees \(0,1,2\);
their geometric pullback and transfer factors are again \((1,1,n)\) and
\((n,n,1)\). This follows from the actual local support complex
\([V_p\to A\to0 A]\), the local angular degree \(n\), and (GTR2.4) with
supports. On the punctured sphere the factors in degrees \(0,1\) are
\((1,n)\) and \((n,1)\). These maps commute with the entire CSP
localization sequence: the maps \(Q^2\to Q\),
\((x_+,x_-)\mapsto x_+-x_-\), have transfer factor \(n\) on both sides;
the maps \(A\to A^2\to A\), \(a\mapsto(-a,a)\mapsto c_++c_-\), have
factor one throughout their degree-two terms. The endpoint map has
factor \(n\). Thus every support sign and both endpoint kernels survive
the transfer.

\section{GTR4. The inverse coefficient map and the two different
adjoints}\label{gtr4.-the-inverse-coefficient-map-and-the-two-different-adjoints}

The already constructed coefficient action is \[
T_a b(u)=b(u/a),
\] \[
\rho_+(a)(f,c_0,c_1)=(f(\cdot/a),c_0,ac_1),\quad
\rho_-(a)(h,d_0,d_1)=(a h(a\,\cdot),ad_0,d_1),
\quad a>0.
\tag{GTR4.1}
\] Direct substitution proves that their inverses are the same displayed
formulas at \(a^{-1}\); they commute with the restrictions as
\(r_p\rho_p(a)=T_ar_p\). This inverse is on coefficient spaces, not on
the geometric cover. It is also the required coefficient map on the
dual: evaluation satisfies \(\lambda(\rho(a)^{-1}\rho(a)x)=\lambda(x)\).
Separation of evaluation proves uniqueness of that coefficient dual map
if evaluation is to be preserved.

Set \(\rho(a)=\rho_+(a)\oplus\rho_-(a)\). The full pullback from CSP is
\[
\mathsf B_n=(\rho(n),T_n,nT_n)
\tag{GTR4.2}
\] on degrees \(0,1,2\). Combine the actual geometric transfer with the
proved inverse coefficient action. Its compatible coefficient
representative is \[
\mathsf U_n=(n\rho(n^{-1}),\ nT_{n^{-1}},\ T_{n^{-1}}).
\tag{GTR4.3}
\] The order of these two operations is immaterial, since the trace is
natural in coefficient maps. On each degree of the displayed complex, \[
\boxed{\mathsf U_n\mathsf B_n=\mathsf B_n\mathsf U_n=n\,1.}
\tag{GTR4.4}
\] The scalar \(n\) therefore comes from the full ramified transfer,
rather than being chosen to obtain a desired spectral formula.
Composition of covers and coefficient actions gives
\(\mathsf U_m\mathsf U_n=\mathsf U_{mn}\).

For the continuous dual complex use CDI's actual Hom differential.
Ordinary transposition of a degree-zero cochain map adds no new sign.
There are three specified maps: \[
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
\text{dual degree}&-2&-1&0\\\hline
\mathsf B_n'&nT_n'&T_n'&\rho(n)'\\
(\mathsf B_n^{-1})'&n^{-1}T_{n^{-1}}'&T_{n^{-1}}'&\rho(n^{-1})'\\
\mathsf U_n'&T_{n^{-1}}'&nT_{n^{-1}}'&n\rho(n^{-1})'.
\end{array}
\tag{GTR4.5}
\] The first is adjoint to original pullback; the second is the
contragredient; the third is adjoint to the constructed transfer with
inverse coefficients. Thus \[
\mathsf U_n'=n(\mathsf B_n^{-1})',\quad
\mathsf B_n'\mathsf U_n'=\mathsf U_n'\mathsf B_n'=n\,1,
\] \[
\langle\mathsf U_n'\lambda,\mathsf B_nx\rangle
=n\langle\lambda,x\rangle.
\tag{GTR4.6}
\] All identities hold on the complete coefficient complex and hence on
its actual cohomology. They do not require a spectral decomposition or a
density assertion. The induced degree-zero dual endpoint characters of
\(\mathsf U_n'\) are \(n,1,1,n\), in the retained order
\(c_0,c_1,d_0,d_1\).

\section{GTR5. The original-zeta residue map receives this exact
transfer
action}\label{gtr5.-the-original-zeta-residue-map-receives-this-exact-transfer-action}

Retain the original Mellin comparison \[
\Theta b(s)=\frac12\int_0^\infty b(u)u^s\,\frac{du}{u},\qquad
\Theta T_n b(s)=n^s\Theta b(s),\qquad \Theta J=\mathcal I.
\tag{GTR5.1}
\] Here \(\mathcal B\) is the entire functions rapidly decreasing on
every bounded real strip, \(\mathcal I\) consists of all functions
vanishing to the actual full multiplicity at every nontrivial zero of
original \(\zeta\), and \(\mathcal Q=\mathcal B/\mathcal I\). Write
\(\kappa:Q\to\mathcal Q\), \([b]\mapsto[\Theta b]\). For \(g=[G]\) with
finitely supported full zero jets, RD proves \[
\iota(g)([F])=\sum_{\rho}\operatorname{Res}_{s=\rho}
\frac{F(s)G(1-s)}{\zeta(s)}\,ds.
\tag{GTR5.2}
\] Each member of this finite-jet subspace has a representative
satisfying the required vanishing at every other zero; it is not a
cutoff of the underlying arithmetic. RD constructs those
representatives, proves that the sum is finite, and proves invertibility
of every local multiplicity matrix. Its map \(\iota\) is a linear
isomorphism onto the finite-jet dual inside the entire continuous dual.

The constructed transfer on degree one is \(nT_{n^{-1}}\); hence its
transpose on \(H^{-1}(D^\vee)=Q'\) is \(nT_{n^{-1}}'\). Substituting in
the complete residue integrand gives \[
\boxed{\kappa'\iota\,T_n
=\mathsf U_n'\,\kappa'\iota.}
\tag{GTR5.3}
\] Indeed replacing \(G(1-s)\) by \(n^{1-s}G(1-s)\) is exactly
multiplying the first argument by \(n^{-s}\) and the result by \(n\).
This proves the diagram with the actual geometric transfer. The factor
in RD5 is now received by a constructed sheaf operation, rather than
merely compared as an identical scalar.

For Taylor-coefficient functionals
\(\delta_{\rho,j}([F])=F^{(j)}(\rho)/j!\), the whole formula is \[
\mathsf U_n'\kappa'\delta_{\rho,j}
=n^{1-\rho}\sum_{h=0}^j
\frac{(-\log n)^{j-h}}{(j-h)!}\kappa'\delta_{\rho,h}.
\tag{GTR5.4}
\] It follows by Taylor multiplication, retaining every nilpotent entry
and factorial. No zero simplicity is assumed. The finite-jet image is
invariant, and \(\mathsf U_n'\) is continuous for the weak topology:
evaluation at \(x\) after transposition is evaluation at the already
constructed \(\mathsf U_nx\). Consequently RD's weakly dense receiver
and its actual ambient continuous dual carry compatible transfer
actions. This does not replace that ambient dual by its completion.

The geometric construction applies to every recovered \(n\ge1\). The
corresponding formulas for arbitrary \(a>0\) define the already
available continuous coefficient representation; no nonintegral
holomorphic cover is asserted.

\section{GTR6. Normal direction, winding orientation and the retained
extra
factors}\label{gtr6.-normal-direction-winding-orientation-and-the-retained-extra-factors}

The primal normal action on \(H^2\) is \(nT_n\) on \(A\). Write
\(T_a^A\) and \(T_a^Q\) when distinguishing the coefficient space from
its quotient, and retain \(q:A\to Q\). Since \(qT_a^A=T_a^Qq\),
transposition gives \((T_a^A)'q'=q'(T_a^Q)'\). The specified three maps
are \[
\mathsf S_{\mathrm{res}}=n(T_{n^{-1}}^Q)'\quad\text{on }Q',\qquad
\mathsf N_{\mathrm{contra}}=n^{-1}(T_{n^{-1}}^A)'\quad\text{on }A',\qquad
\mathsf N_{\mathrm{transfer}}=(T_{n^{-1}}^A)'\quad\text{on }A'.
\] Their exact comparison, with its domain and receiving inclusion
retained, is \[
q'\mathsf S_{\mathrm{res}}
=n^2\mathsf N_{\mathrm{contra}}q'
=n\mathsf N_{\mathrm{transfer}}q':Q'\longrightarrow A'.
\tag{GTR6.0}
\] Here \(q'\) identifies \(Q'\) with \(J^\perp\); SDT5 proves this is
also a closed strong topological embedding. Thus the residue action has
the displayed extra factors on this specific subspace of the full normal
dual, not on every functional in \(A'\). None of the factors or the
inclusion may be removed.

CDW's winding coordinate \(a[\vartheta]\) maps to \(-a\) in positive
sphere integration. Under that comparison, the GSL normal map is exactly
\[
a[\vartheta]\longmapsto
-[(1-E_+(s))(\Theta a)(s-1)]_{\mathcal I\cap\mathcal I_+},
\tag{GTR6.1}
\] with kernel \(J[\vartheta]\). The sign commutes with both \(nT_n\)
and \(T_{n^{-1}}\), so the trace and pullback tables are unchanged by
this explicit coordinate comparison. It is not permission to omit the
sign from the normal map itself.

The two covers' pole trace maps remain separate. Likewise the
holomorphic swap \(-1/z\) and antiholomorphic swap \(-1/\overline z\)
retain their original CDW angular signs \(-1,+1\) and their CSP
degree-two signs \(+1,-1\). Their current pushforwards are adjoints to
their specified pullbacks. No positive degree is assigned to the
antiholomorphic orientation reversal by (GTR3.2), which concerns only
the holomorphic covers \(b_n\).

\section{GTR7. Naturality with the actual lifting
boundary}\label{gtr7.-naturality-with-the-actual-lifting-boundary}

The exact source sequence is \[
0\longrightarrow\mathscr F_J\longrightarrow\mathscr F
\longrightarrow j_!\underline Q\longrightarrow0.
\tag{GTR7.1}
\] The weighted trace is defined on all three terms by the same fibre
multiplicities and is natural in their coefficient maps by GTR2.
Therefore its induced long exact sequences commute with transfer, as
they do with pullback. For the actual connecting map \[

the specified coefficient actions are invertible. Thus the new trace
construction does not falsely add an independent restriction to the
lifting problem. CW4 and CW7 prove \(\delta=0\) on the entire source;
the present construction proves how this already established lift is
carried through the actual geometric trace and its continuous dual.

The identity (GTR5.4) pairs actual exponents \(\rho\) and \(1-\rho\)

\section{GTR10. The completed residue receiver and the full trace

The completed strong-topology proof SDT0--SDT9 was read in full. Its

Define the residue seminorms on the already constructed finite-support

p_B^{\mathrm{res}}(G)=\sup_{F\in B}\left|
\sum_\rho\operatorname{Res}_{s=\rho}
\frac{F(s)G(1-s)}{\zeta(s)}\,ds\right|,

=\widehat{(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{fin}},(p_B^{\mathrm{res}})_B)}.

\] This names the specified Hausdorff completion, not a new topology

\widehat\iota:\mathcal H_{\mathrm{res}}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal Q'_\beta,
\qquad
\mathfrak I=\kappa'\widehat\iota:

Each defining strong seminorm therefore pulls back to the seminorm on
the corresponding bounded image. This proves both directions of the

For every \(a>0\), put \(\mathsf V_a=aT_{a^{-1}}\) on
\(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{fin}}\). Direct substitution into the full

p_B^{\mathrm{res}}(T_aG)
=a\,p_{T_{a^{-1}}B}^{\mathrm{res}}(G),\qquad
p_B^{\mathrm{res}}(\mathsf V_aG)
=p_{T_aB}^{\mathrm{res}}(G).
\tag{GTR10.4}

\widehat T_a\widehat T_b=\widehat T_{ab},\qquad
\widehat{\mathsf V}_a\widehat{\mathsf V}_b
=\widehat{\mathsf V}_{ab},\qquad
\widehat T_a\widehat{\mathsf V}_a=a\,1.
\tag{GTR10.5}

\boxed{
\mathfrak I\widehat T_n=\mathsf U_n'\mathfrak I,
\qquad

The complete pairing is the actual evaluation \[
\widehat{\mathcal R}(F,h)=\widehat\iota(h)(F),
\qquad F\in\mathcal Q,\ h\in\mathcal H_{\mathrm{res}}.
\tag{GTR10.7}

The full transfer identities become \[

Finally, the actual two-support restriction in degree minus one is \[

\section{GTR11. Identification of the actual trace on the derived direct
image}\label{gtr11.-identification-of-the-actual-trace-on-the-derived-direct-image}

There is a stronger receiving statement than the cohomology calculation
of GTR3. Work in the ordinary derived category of complex vector-space
sheaves on the actual three-point space \(X\). CDW4 constructs the
specific quasi-isomorphism \[
\Phi:\Omega\oplus\mathscr W[-1]\xrightarrow{\sim}R\pi_*\mathscr F,
\qquad \mathscr W=j_{\eta!}\underline A_{\{\eta\}},
\tag{GTR11.1}
\] represented by constants and the positive angular form. Here
\(\mathscr W\) is a sheaf on \(X\), not the previously used vector space
\(W=V_+\oplus V_-\). Its only nonzero stalk is \(A\) at \(\eta\). Every
map in the stated representative is continuous on the original
coefficient spaces. CDW5 proves, before taking global cohomology, that
geometric pullback \(P_n\) obeys \[
P_n\Phi=\Phi\begin{pmatrix}1_{\Omega}&0\\0&n1_{\mathscr W[-1]}\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{GTR11.2}
\] Consequently \(P_n\) is an automorphism of this actual derived direct
image. Its inverse is represented through \(\Phi\) by
\(\operatorname{diag}(1,n^{-1})\); no inverse geometric root map is
used.

Let \(\mathsf t_n\) be the morphism on \(R\pi_*\mathscr F\) induced by
the actual sheaf trace of GTR2. Since \(\pi b_n=\pi\), the intermediate
object \(R\pi_*b_{n*}\mathscr F\) is canonically \(R\pi_*\mathscr F\).
To justify this derived identification, \(b_{n*}\) is exact by GTR2 and
preserves injectives because it is right adjoint to the exact
inverse-image functor. An injective resolution therefore computes both
sides of the composite direct image. The sheaf equality (GTR2.4) yields
the equality of derived morphisms \[
\mathsf t_nP_n=n\,1_{R\pi_*\mathscr F}.
\tag{GTR11.3}
\] Explicitly, for the preceding identification
\(\alpha:R\pi_*b_{n*}\mathscr F\xrightarrow{\sim}R\pi_*\mathscr F\), the
two maps are \(P_n=\alpha\,R\pi_*(u_n)\) and
\(\mathsf t_n=R\pi_*(\operatorname{Tr}_n)\alpha^{-1}\). CDW's chain
pullback extends the sheaf unit through its augmentation; it therefore
represents this same \(P_n\). Compose on the right with the already
constructed inverse of \(P_n\). This proves \[
\boxed{
\mathsf t_n=nP_n^{-1},\qquad
\mathsf t_n\Phi
=\Phi\begin{pmatrix}n1_{\Omega}&0\\0&1_{\mathscr W[-1]}\end{pmatrix}.}
\tag{GTR11.4}
\] This identifies the actual trace morphism in the derived category,
including its possible extension information. It does not infer equality
of morphisms merely from equal induced cohomology maps.

The coefficient action of (GTR4.1) commutes with \(\Phi\), preserves
both summands, and has an explicit inverse. Thus the combined pullback
and inverse-coefficient transfer are represented on (GTR11.1) by \[
\mathsf B_n=
\begin{pmatrix}\rho_{\Omega}(n)&0\\0&nT_n\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\mathsf U_n=
\begin{pmatrix}n\rho_{\Omega}(n^{-1})&0\\0&T_{n^{-1}}\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{GTR11.5}
\] The sheaf morphism \(\rho_{\Omega}(a)\) means
\(\rho_+(a),\rho_-(a),T_a\) on the two chart stalks and the generic

sections and the simultaneous contractions of CW2 gives exactly the full

\(n\) comes from the \(\Omega\) summand's trace, while the degree-two

the angular coordinate and positive sphere integration remains in that
comparison.

Every step is natural in the diagrams for \(J\to A\to Q\), since CDW8's
\(\Phi\) is natural and the trace was constructed naturally in GTR2.
Thus the same derived identification applies simultaneously to the
actual source sequence (GTR7.1), with its boundary maps, rather than to

\chapter{The actual algebraic Verdier dual and its continuous
coefficient
comparison}\label{the-actual-algebraic-verdier-dual-and-its-continuous-coefficient-comparison}

Independent mathematical derivation, 24 September 2026. Proof locators
VSD0--VSD14.

\section{VSD0. Input, categories, and
prerequisites}\label{vsd0.-input-categories-and-prerequisites}

This calculation takes place after the complete arithmetic
reconstruction. The user's notation \(Z_0,Z_1,\ldots,\tau\) is
unchanged. There is no addition, numerical coordinate, distance, or
parity operation on \(\tau\) here. The coefficient spaces and their
scalar operations are the already constructed receiving objects of CSP
and CDI. Dualization is an operation on those coefficients, not a new
construction of the counting unit or of selected primes.

The corpus rule argument\_reconstruction/CORPUS\_AND\_OPERATION\_RULE.md
was read. The complete coefficient-dual proof CDI0--CDI12 and complete
original-zeta residue proof RD0--RD9 were read. CSP0--CSP7, including
the inverse-image sheaf, finite complexes, local orientations and
support maps, were read in full. CDW9--CDW10's positive-integration and
original-zeta comparisons were also read. This is an independent
calculation of their sheaf-duality receiver, not a claimed new reading
of the entire original Connes--Consani or Deligne papers.

Let \(Y=\mathbb P^1(\mathbb C)\) have its usual topology and positive
complex orientation. Write \(D=\{p_+,p_-\}=\{0,\infty\}\),
\(i:D\hookrightarrow Y\), and \(j:U=Y\setminus D\hookrightarrow Y\).
Retain \[
A,\quad J=\Sigma S\subset A,\quad Q=A/J,\quad
V_p=S\oplus E_p,\quad E_p=\mathbb C^2,\quad r_p:V_p\to A.
\tag{VSD0.1}
\] Here \(r_+=\Sigma\), \(r_-=R\Sigma=\Sigma\widehat{\phantom f}\) on
the source summands, and both vanish on the stated endpoint summands.
SSI and CDI1 prove that \(J\) is closed, \(\Sigma:S\to J\) is a
topological isomorphism, and continuous sections \(s_p:J\to V_p\)
satisfy \[
r_ps_p=1_J,\qquad V_p\simeq J\oplus E_p.
\tag{VSD0.2}
\] These coefficient spaces are Hausdorff Fréchet spaces. Put \[
W=V_+\oplus V_-,\quad d(v_+,v_-)=r_+v_+-r_-v_-,
\quad Z=\ker d\simeq J\oplus E_+\oplus E_-.
\tag{VSD0.3}
\] The actual sheaf is \[
\mathscr F=\underline A_Y\times_{i_*(A\oplus A)}i_*W,
\tag{VSD0.4}
\] with exact presentation \[
0\to\mathscr F\to\underline A_Y\oplus i_*W
\xrightarrow{\epsilon-r}i_*(A\oplus A)\to0.
\tag{VSD0.5}
\] The two output components are \(a|_{p_+}-r_+v_+\) and
\(a|_{p_-}-r_-v_-\). Surjectivity is stalkwise using the constant-sheaf
coordinate at the chosen pole.

Our ordinary sheaf category is the abelian category of sheaves of
complex vector spaces. It imposes no continuity on coefficient linear
maps. Distinguish \[
E^*=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(E,\mathbb C),\qquad
E'=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cont},\mathbb C}(E,\mathbb C),\qquad
E^\dagger=E^*/E'.
\tag{VSD0.6}
\] The first is the full algebraic dual, the second the continuous dual
with weak topology when needed, and the third initially only a vector
space. No finite-dimensional or reflexive hypothesis is inserted.

Complexes are cohomological: \((C[k])^n=C^{n+k}\), so
\(\underline E[2]\) has its coefficient in degree \(-2\). Our Hom
differential and cone differential are \[
d_{C^*}^{\,n}\lambda=(-1)^{n+1}\lambda d_C^{-n-1},
\qquad d_{\operatorname{Cone}(f)}(b,a)=(d_Bb+f(a),-d_Aa).
\tag{VSD0.7}
\]

\section{VSD1. Constant coefficients of arbitrary
dimension}\label{vsd1.-constant-coefficients-of-arbitrary-dimension}

The dualizing complex on the oriented real two-manifold \(Y\) is \[
\omega_Y=\underline{\mathbb C}_Y[2].
\tag{VSD1.1}
\] Its orientation is fixed by integration of a compactly supported
two-form with positive integral one in each positive complex coordinate.
The local compact-support de Rham calculation on an oriented disk gives
one coefficient in degree two and zero in the other degrees; extension
by zero and integration give the trace map. These local orientation
identifications glue to the displayed dualizing complex. Neither pole
orientation is reversed.

Define ordinary Verdier duality by \[
\mathbb D_Y K=R\mathcal Hom_Y(K,\omega_Y).
\tag{VSD1.2}
\] For every vector space \(E\), including arbitrary infinite dimension,
\[
\boxed{\mathbb D_Y\underline E_Y\simeq\underline{E^*}_Y[2].}
\tag{VSD1.3}
\] To verify the coefficient claim without finite rank, on any open disk
\(B\) constant-sheaf adjunction gives \[
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Sh}(B)}(\underline E_B,K)
=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(E,\Gamma(B,K)).
\tag{VSD1.4}
\] A sheaf map is determined by the images of constant sections;
conversely a linear map into sections extends to locally constant
sections by gluing on their regions of constancy. Resolve \(K\) by
injective sheaves. Vector-space Hom from \(E\) is exact: choose a basis
and lift each basis image through any surjection. The Hom complex
therefore has cohomology \[
\operatorname{Ext}_{\mathrm{Sh}(B)}^q(\underline E_B,K)
=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(E,H^q(B,K)).
\tag{VSD1.5}
\] For constant \(K=\underline{\mathbb C}_B\), the disk contraction
gives \(H^0=\mathbb C\), \(H^{q>0}=0\). Internal derived-Hom stalks are
the filtered colimit of these local Ext groups; higher internal Ext
stalks vanish. In degree zero the internal Hom is constant with
coefficient \(E^*\): on a connected disk each scalar image of a constant
section is constant, defining a single linear functional on all of
\(E\). Thus (VSD1.3) follows.

For a point \(p\) and every vector space \(B\), \[
i_p^!\underline B_Y=B[-2],\qquad i_p^!\underline B_Y[2]=B.
\tag{VSD1.6}
\] Indeed the disk/punctured-disk relative complex has identity
restriction in degree zero, while the punctured disk has its independent
degree-one angular coefficient \(B\). Its fibre is the local fundamental
class in degree two. This is the coefficient version of CSP6 and uses no
dimension bound.

\section{VSD2. Pole duals and the signed Gysin
map}\label{vsd2.-pole-duals-and-the-signed-gysin-map}

For a skyscraper coefficient, \[
\boxed{\mathbb D_Yi_{p*}E=i_{p*}E^*.}
\tag{VSD2.1}
\] Closed-inclusion adjunction identifies derived Hom from \(i_{p*}E\)
into \(\omega_Y\) with the pushforward of derived Hom from \(E\) into
\(i_p^!\omega_Y=\mathbb C\). At the point vector-space Hom is exact, so
no higher Ext remains. This proves (VSD2.1) in arbitrary dimension.

For any vector space \(B\), define \[
g_{p,B}:i_{p*}B\longrightarrow\underline B_Y[2]
\tag{VSD2.2}
\] as the adjunction counit corresponding to the identity of
\(B=i_p^!\underline B_Y[2]\), where the identification is positive local
complex orientation. Derived adjunction specifies this fully: \[
\operatorname{Hom}_{D(Y)}(i_{p*}B,\underline B_Y[2])
=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(B,B).
\tag{VSD2.3}
\] The dual of restriction \(\underline E_Y\to i_{p*}E\) is
\(g_{p,E^*}\) with positive sign. To check it, pair \(e\) with
\(\lambda\); the corresponding local compactly supported two-form has
integral \(\lambda(e)\), using a positive fundamental form. Extension by
zero to the sphere preserves that integral, so the global scalar is
\(+\lambda(e)\).

The angular connecting sign is separate. For \(\chi=1\) near the pole
and zero outside a disk, \[
-d\chi\wedge\frac{d\theta_p}{2\pi},
\qquad \int -d\chi\wedge\frac{d\theta_p}{2\pi}=1
\tag{VSD2.4}
\] is positive local orientation. In the CSP relative cone the boundary
of the positive angular class is the negative of this positive-integral
class. Gysin then carries the positive fundamental class positively to
the global one. These signs belong to different maps.

For the two poles, \[
g_B=g_{p_+,B}+g_{p_-,B}:i_*(B\oplus B)\to\underline B_Y[2]
\tag{VSD2.5}
\] induces \[
B\oplus B\to H^0(Y,\underline B[2])=B,
\qquad(b_+,b_-)\mapsto b_++b_-.
\tag{VSD2.6}
\] Both local coordinates \(z,w=1/z\) are complex oriented. The identity
\(d\arg w=-d\arg z\) belongs to the annular comparison, not to the Gysin
sum.

\section{VSD3. The actual algebraic Verdier
triangle}\label{vsd3.-the-actual-algebraic-verdier-triangle}

Dualizing (VSD0.5) with those explicitly computed maps gives \[
i_*((A^*)^2)\xrightarrow{(g_{A^*},-r^*)}
\underline{A^*}_Y[2]\oplus i_*W^*
\longrightarrow\mathbb D_Y\mathscr F
\longrightarrow i_*((A^*)^2)[1].
\tag{VSD3.1}
\] The restriction component is \[
(\lambda_+,\lambda_-)\mapsto
(-r_+^*\lambda_+,-r_-^*\lambda_-).
\tag{VSD3.2}
\] It retains the minus in \(\epsilon-r\); Gysin retains the positive
sign of \(\epsilon\). Thus, representing the Gysin maps on a resolution
when forming a cone, \[
\boxed{\mathbb D_Y\mathscr F\simeq
\operatorname{Cone}\left(
i_*((A^*)^2)\xrightarrow{(g_{A^*},-r^*)}
\underline{A^*}_Y[2]\oplus i_*W^*\right).}
\tag{VSD3.3}
\] This constructs the sheaf dual. It does not declare that a
continuous-dual complex is already the ordinary Verdier dual.

\section{VSD4. Every stalk and
costalk}\label{vsd4.-every-stalk-and-costalk}

On the interior, \[
j^*\mathbb D_Y\mathscr F=\underline{A^*}_U[2].
\tag{VSD4.1}
\] At a pole the derived stalk of Gysin is zero as a derived
vector-space map from degree zero to degree minus two: vector-space Ext
in degree two is zero. In the local cone, multiplying the
degree-minus-one source coordinate by minus one turns \(-r_p^*\) into
\(+r_p^*\). The stalk model is \[
A^*\ \text{in degree }-2,\qquad
A^*\xrightarrow{r_p^*}V_p^*
\ \text{in degrees }-1,0.
\tag{VSD4.2}
\] It is the transpose of CSP's positive-integration costalk
\(L_p=[V_p\to^{r_p}A\to^0A]\). Vanishing of the stalk Gysin map does not
make the global Gysin morphism vanish.

The algebraic dual restriction sequence is exact: \[
0\to Q^*\xrightarrow{q^*}A^*\to J^*\to0.
\tag{VSD4.3}
\] Surjectivity follows by extending a basis of \(J\) to one of \(A\).
Since \(V_p=J\oplus E_p\), the image of \(r_p^*\) is precisely the
annihilator of \(E_p\). Thus \[
\mathcal H^{-2}(\mathbb D\mathscr F)_p=A^*,\quad
\mathcal H^{-1}(\mathbb D\mathscr F)_p=Q^*,\quad
\mathcal H^0(\mathbb D\mathscr F)_p=E_p^*.
\tag{VSD4.4}
\] All other pole cohomology stalks vanish. The full cohomology sheaves
are \[
\mathcal H^{-2}(\mathbb D\mathscr F)=\underline{A^*}_Y,\quad
\mathcal H^{-1}(\mathbb D\mathscr F)=i_*(Q^*\oplus Q^*),\quad
\mathcal H^0(\mathbb D\mathscr F)=i_*(E_+^*\oplus E_-^*).
\tag{VSD4.5}
\] Degree-minus-two generization is identity. This list does not replace
the cone and its Gysin extension class.

Applying \(i_p^!\) to (VSD3.1), the map becomes \[
A^*\to A^*\oplus V_p^*,\qquad
\lambda\mapsto(\lambda,-r_p^*\lambda).
\tag{VSD4.6}
\] Its cone contracts to \(V_p^*[0]\). Explicitly the projection \[
(a,\phi)\longmapsto\phi+r_p^*a
\tag{VSD4.7}
\] is onto with kernel precisely (VSD4.6). Therefore \[
\boxed{i_p^!\mathbb D_Y\mathscr F\simeq V_p^*[0].}
\tag{VSD4.8}
\] At an interior point \(x\), \(i_x^!\mathbb D\mathscr F=A^*[0]\). Both
stalk/costalk interchange statements are established by these actual
local complexes.

\section{VSD5. Global cohomology and explicit
contraction}\label{vsd5.-global-cohomology-and-explicit-contraction}

Derived global sections of (VSD3.3) have finite model \[
K_*^{-2}=A^*,\quad K_*^{-1}=(A^*)^2,\quad K_*^0=A^*\oplus V_+^*\oplus V_-^*,
\] \[
d^{-2}=0,\quad
d^{-1}(\lambda_+,\lambda_-)
=(\lambda_++\lambda_-,-r_+^*\lambda_+,-r_-^*\lambda_-).
\tag{VSD5.1}
\] The degree-minus-two coefficient comes from sphere degree zero of the
unshifted constant sheaf. The degree-zero \(A^*\) comes from its
positive sphere degree-two class; its two Gysin contributions are the
sum in (VSD2.6). This is precisely the algebraic Hom complex of CSP4.1.

It contracts onto \[
D_*^{-2}=A^*,\quad D_*^{-1}=A^*,\quad D_*^0=V_+^*\oplus V_-^*,\qquad
d^{-2}=0,\quad d^{-1}\lambda=(r_+^*\lambda,-r_-^*\lambda).
\tag{VSD5.2}
\] The inclusion \(u:D_*\to K_*\) and retraction \(v:K_*\to D_*\) are \[
u^{-2}=1,\quad u^{-1}\lambda=(-\lambda,\lambda),\quad
u^0(\phi_+,\phi_-)=(0,\phi_+,\phi_-),
\tag{VSD5.3}
\] \[
v^{-2}=1,\quad v^{-1}(\lambda_+,\lambda_-)=-\lambda_+,\quad
v^0(a,\phi_+,\phi_-)=(\phi_+,\phi_-+r_-^*a).
\tag{VSD5.4}
\] Substitution shows they are chain maps and \(vu=1\). A homotopy for
\(1-uv\) is \[
h^0(a,\phi_+,\phi_-)=(0,a)
\tag{VSD5.5}
\] with all other components zero: \(dh\) in degree zero is
\((a,0,-r_-^*a)\), and \(hd\) in degree minus one is
\((0,\lambda_++\lambda_-)\), exactly \(1-uv\).

Since \(W\simeq Z\oplus J\) by CDI1's explicit section, restriction and
extension of algebraic functionals give \[
\boxed{H^{-2}(Y,\mathbb D\mathscr F)=A^*,\quad
H^{-1}(Y,\mathbb D\mathscr F)=Q^*,\quad
H^0(Y,\mathbb D\mathscr F)=Z^*.}
\tag{VSD5.6}
\] Their pairings with CSP's \(A,Q,Z\) are ordinary evaluation on each
full algebraic dual. No bidual surjectivity is asserted.

\section{VSD6. The complete transposed support
maps}\label{vsd6.-the-complete-transposed-support-maps}

The source support map has components

\[
k^0=1_W,\quad k^1(b_+,b_-)=b_+-b_-,\quad
k^2(c_+,c_-)=c_++c_-.
\tag{VSD6.1}
\] Under the exact local and global dual models, restriction of the dual
global complex to the two dual stalk models is \[
(k^*)^0=1_{W^*},\qquad
(k^*)^{-1}\lambda=(\lambda,-\lambda),\qquad
(k^*)^{-2}\lambda=(\lambda,\lambda).
\tag{VSD6.2}
\] The pole differential sends \((\lambda_+,\lambda_-)\) to
\((r_+^*\lambda_+,r_-^*\lambda_-)\), so chain compatibility follows
directly. The cohomology maps are diagonal on \(A^*\), anti-diagonal on
\(Q^*\), and endpoint restriction on \(Z^*\).

The complete nonzero part of the algebraically dual localization row is
\[
\begin{aligned}
0\to A^*&\xrightarrow{\lambda\mapsto(\lambda,\lambda)}(A^*)^2
\xrightarrow{(\lambda_+,\lambda_-)\mapsto-\lambda_++\lambda_-}A^*
\xrightarrow{0}Q^*\\
&\xrightarrow{\mu\mapsto(\mu,-\mu)}(Q^*)^2
\xrightarrow{(\mu_+,\mu_-)\mapsto q^*(\mu_++\mu_-)}A^*
\xrightarrow{r^*}Z^*
\xrightarrow{\mathrm{res}}E_+^*\oplus E_-^*\to0 .
\end{aligned}
\tag{VSD6.3}
\] Here \(r:Z\to A\) is common restriction and
\(r^*\lambda=(\lambda|_J,0,0)\). Exactness follows from the displayed
sum/difference kernels, \(\ker(A^*\to J^*)=q^*Q^*\), extension onto
\(J^*\), and the split endpoint coordinates. The annular arrow is the
transpose of \(a\mapsto(-a,a)\); it is not the transpose of the Gysin
sum.

There is also the support-to-global map for the dual sheaf itself. Its
two pole costalks, computed in (VSD4.8), are
\(V_+^*[0]\oplus V_-^*[0]\). On the global model (VSD5.2) their
inclusion is the identity into degree zero \(W^*\). On cohomology this
is restriction of a functional on \(W\) to its subspace \(Z\). Thus \[
(\phi_+,\phi_-)\longmapsto
\bigl(s_+^*\phi_++s_-^*\phi_-,\,
\phi_+|_{E_+},\,\phi_-|_{E_-}\bigr)
\quad\text{in }Z^*\simeq J^*\oplus E_+^*\oplus E_-^*.
\tag{VSD6.4}
\] Both pole contributions have a positive sign. Its kernel is precisely
\(\{(r_+^*\lambda,-r_-^*\lambda):\lambda\in A^*\}\): it consists of the
functionals annihilating \(Z\), which factor through \(d:W\to J\), and
every such functional on \(J\) extends to \(A\). Surjectivity follows
from the explicit splitting \(W\simeq Z\oplus J\). Hence (VSD6.4) is
also completely calculated; it is a different map from the
dual-global-to-dual-stalk restriction in (VSD6.2).

\section{VSD7. A continuous subcomparison as an actual sheaf
object}\label{vsd7.-a-continuous-subcomparison-as-an-actual-sheaf-object}

The continuous candidate is constructed in the same ordinary derived
sheaf category, with the specified continuous-dual coefficient
subspaces: \[
\mathscr D_c\mathscr F=
\operatorname{Cone}\left(
i_*((A')^2)\xrightarrow{(g_{A'},-r')}
\underline{A'}_Y[2]\oplus i_*W'\right).
\tag{VSD7.1}
\] This defines actual constant and skyscraper sheaves, using the
constructed Gysin map and continuous transposes. It is not asserted to
be a general dualizing functor on all topological sheaves. It supplies
an actual receiving object for this particular \(\mathscr F\).

The inclusions \(E'\hookrightarrow E^*\) commute with all transposes.
Gysin is coefficient-natural by its identity characterization (VSD2.3).
They therefore produce \[
\boxed{c:\mathscr D_c\mathscr F\longrightarrow\mathbb D_Y\mathscr F.}
\tag{VSD7.2}
\] The functorial resolution of the coefficient-natural Gysin diagrams
produces a map of ordinary cone complexes, so (VSD7.2) is not merely a
comparison between cohomology lists.

The preceding finite calculations hold with primes instead of stars.
Continuous Hahn--Banach on the closed subspace \(J\subset A\) supplies
the required surjectivity of restriction; CDI1 proves that step with
these actual topologies. Consequently \[
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
 &-2&-1&0\\ \hline
H^\bullet(Y,\mathscr D_c\mathscr F)&A'&Q'&Z'\\
\mathcal H^\bullet(\mathscr D_c\mathscr F)_p&A'&Q'&E_p'
\end{array}
\tag{VSD7.3}
\] and \(i_p^!\mathscr D_c\mathscr F=V_p'[0]\); the interior restriction
is \(\underline{A'}[2]\). The global finite complex is exactly CDI2.2,
the pole complex CDI2.6, and support maps are CDI4--CDI5. Each
cohomology map of \(c\) is the inclusion of continuous into full
algebraic dual of the corresponding original group. With weak
coefficient topologies the finite-model cohomology topologies are the
exact weak topologies proved in CDI3. The ordinary sheaf category
records the underlying vector spaces.

Thus the continuous coefficient model now has an actual sheaf receiver,
with a proved map to ordinary Verdier duality. The two duals have not
been identified without a map.

\section{VSD8. The comparison cone and every one of its
groups}\label{vsd8.-the-comparison-cone-and-every-one-of-its-groups}

Write \[
\mathscr E=\operatorname{Cone}(c).
\tag{VSD8.1}
\] The exact comparison object is \[
\boxed{\mathscr E\simeq
\operatorname{Cone}\left(
i_*((A^\dagger)^2)\xrightarrow{(g_{A^\dagger},-r^\dagger)}
\underline{A^\dagger}_Y[2]\oplus i_*W^\dagger
\right).}
\tag{VSD8.2}
\] For each coefficient, \(0\to E'\to E^*\to E^\dagger\to0\) induces
exact sequences of constant sheaves and skyscrapers, since exactness is
stalkwise. The coefficient-natural Gysin square gives a morphism of
triangles. Its cone is (VSD8.2): one may compute it by functorial
resolutions and the two cone differentials, or by the resulting exact
quotient diagram. No topology on \(E^\dagger\) is used here.

The continuous and algebraic restriction rows form the exact diagram \[
\begin{array}{ccccccccc}
0&\to&Q'&\to&A'&\to&J'&\to&0\\
&&\downarrow&&\downarrow&&\downarrow\\
0&\to&Q^*&\to&A^*&\to&J^*&\to&0 .
\end{array}
\tag{VSD8.3}
\] All vertical maps are injections. The quotient row is therefore \[
0\to Q^\dagger\to A^\dagger\to J^\dagger\to0 .
\tag{VSD8.4}
\] To verify its middle kernel directly, an algebraic functional on
\(A\) whose restriction to \(J\) is continuous differs, by a continuous
Hahn--Banach extension of that restriction, from a functional factoring
algebraically through \(Q\). Surjectivity on the right follows by
algebraic extension from \(J\).

The endpoint spaces are finite dimensional, so all their functionals are
continuous. The actual splittings in VSD0 give \[
V_p^\dagger\simeq J^\dagger,\qquad
Z^\dagger\simeq J^\dagger,\qquad E_p^\dagger=0 .
\tag{VSD8.5}
\] The induced \(r_p^\dagger:A^\dagger\to V_p^\dagger\) is onto and has
kernel \(Q^\dagger\). The finite complexes now give \[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal H^{-2}(\mathscr E)&=\underline{A^\dagger}_Y,&
\mathcal H^{-1}(\mathscr E)&=i_*(Q^\dagger\oplus Q^\dagger),&
\mathcal H^0(\mathscr E)&=0,\\
i_p^!\mathscr E&=V_p^\dagger[0]\simeq J^\dagger[0],\\
H^{-2}(Y,\mathscr E)&=A^\dagger,&
H^{-1}(Y,\mathscr E)&=Q^\dagger,&
H^0(Y,\mathscr E)&=Z^\dagger\simeq J^\dagger .
\end{aligned}}
\tag{VSD8.6}
\] In particular a zero degree-zero cohomology sheaf does not force zero
degree-zero global cohomology or zero pole costalk. The Gysin extension
in (VSD8.2) retains this information.

All support maps are (VSD6.2)--(VSD6.3) on the dagger coefficients, with
finite endpoint terms zero. This comparison defect has specified
support, maps and computed cohomology; it is not an unnamed failure of
an analogy.

\section{VSD9. Nonzero defect for the actual infinite
coefficients}\label{vsd9.-nonzero-defect-for-the-actual-infinite-coefficients}

Every infinite-dimensional Hausdorff Fréchet space \(E\) has
discontinuous algebraic functionals. For a defining seminorm sequence
\(p_1,p_2,\ldots\), choose independent \(x_n\) and scale them by nonzero
constants to obtain independent \(v_n\) with \[
\max_{1\le j\le n}p_j(v_n)\le2^{-n}.
\tag{VSD9.1}
\] Then \(v_n\to0\). Assign \(\lambda(v_n)=1\) on their span and extend
the independent family to an algebraic basis of \(E\), assigning zero to
the additional basis vectors. This defines an algebraic functional which
is not continuous. Hence \(E^\dagger\ne0\).

The actual \(A\) is infinite dimensional: smooth functions with pairwise
disjoint compact supports in \(\mathbb R_{>0}\) lie in \(A\) and are
independent. The actual \(S\) is infinite dimensional too. In pairwise
disjoint positive intervals choose nonzero compactly supported smooth
functions of integral zero, for example derivatives of interior bump
functions, and extend them evenly. They vanish at zero, retain integral
zero on the real line, and are independent members of \(S\). The proved
topological isomorphism \(\Sigma:S\to J\) gives \[
A^\dagger\ne0,\qquad J^\dagger\ne0.
\tag{VSD9.2}
\] Consequently \(c\) is not a quasi-isomorphism: its open-stratum
degree-minus-two cokernel is the nonzero \(A^\dagger\). Its pole costalk
comparison also has nonzero quotient \(J^\dagger\). This proves the
precise difference between the two defined dual constructions; it says
nothing against the original support \(\tau\) or its lifting programme.

\section{VSD10. Weak completion and the original residue
family}\label{vsd10.-weak-completion-and-the-original-residue-family}

For every Hausdorff locally convex \(E\), \[
\overline{E'}^{\,\sigma(E^*,E)}=E^*.
\tag{VSD10.1}
\] Indeed fix \(\lambda\in E^*\) and finitely many \(e_1,\ldots,e_m\).
On their finite-dimensional span \(L\), the restriction of \(\lambda\)
is continuous, because the Hausdorff induced topology on \(L\) is its
ordinary finite-dimensional topology. It is bounded by a continuous
seminorm induced from \(E\). Hahn--Banach extends it continuously to all
of \(E\), agreeing exactly on the prescribed vectors. Every pointwise
neighborhood of \(\lambda\) therefore meets \(E'\).

The full algebraic dual is complete in pointwise convergence. It is the
closed subspace of the complete product \(\mathbb C^E\) cut out by every
linearity equation \[
f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y),\qquad f(cx)=cf(x).
\tag{VSD10.2}
\] Its topology on \(E'\) is exactly the weak dual topology. Thus \[
\boxed{\text{the Hausdorff completion of }E'_\sigma
\text{ is }E^*\text{ with its pointwise topology}.}
\tag{VSD10.3}
\] Weak completion and weak closure inside a specified continuous dual
are different operations; neither is substituted for the other.

The quotient topology on \(E^*/E'\) from \(\sigma(E^*,E)\) is
indiscrete. To see it, let a nonempty open saturated set contain
\(x+U\), with \(U\) an open neighborhood of zero. For any \(y\), density
makes \(y-x-U\) meet \(E'\), so \(y\in x+U+E'\), and saturation places
every \(y\) in the set. Its only open subsets are therefore empty and
whole. The nonzero algebraic quotients in VSD9 are not Hausdorff
quotients for this particular topology. They remain the exact
ordinary-sheaf coefficients in VSD8.

RD's finite-support original-zeta residue family \(\mathcal D\)
satisfies both \[
\overline{\mathcal D}^{\sigma(\mathcal Q',\mathcal Q)}=\mathcal Q',
\qquad
\overline{\mathcal D}^{\sigma(\mathcal Q^*,\mathcal Q)}=\mathcal Q^* .
\tag{VSD10.4}
\] The first is RD4. For the second, take any algebraic \(\lambda\) and
finitely many \(x_1,\ldots,x_m\in\mathcal Q\). If their
\(\lambda\)-values were outside the finite-dimensional image
\(\{(d(x_i))_i:d\in\mathcal D\}\), a separating linear relation would
annihilate every full zero jet of \(\sum c_ix_i\), hence that class
would be zero by the definition of \(\mathcal Q\), while its
\(\lambda\)-value would be nonzero. This contradiction proves exact
interpolation on every finite set, hence the second density. These
equations have different stated ambient spaces. Neither makes a
discontinuous functional continuous or changes the residue formula.

\section{VSD11. Original-zeta data and receiving
morphisms}\label{vsd11.-original-zeta-data-and-receiving-morphisms}

The actual coefficient comparison remains \[
\kappa:Q\longrightarrow\mathcal Q,\qquad
[a]\longmapsto\left[\frac12\int_0^\infty a(u)u^s\frac{du}{u}\right],
\tag{VSD11.1}
\] with \(\Sigma f=2\sum_{n\ge1}f(nu)\). Its exact dual square is \[
\begin{array}{ccc}
\mathcal Q'&\hookrightarrow&\mathcal Q^*\\
\downarrow\kappa'&&\downarrow\kappa^*\\
Q'&\hookrightarrow&Q^* .
\end{array}
\tag{VSD11.2}
\] Both vertical maps are isomorphisms, and so is the induced map on
their algebraic quotients. RD's finite-support residue map therefore
enters the two sheaf-dual receivers through the actual inclusion: \[
\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{fin}}
\xrightarrow{\kappa'\iota}H^{-1}(Y,\mathscr D_c\mathscr F)
\xrightarrow{H^{-1}(c)}H^{-1}(Y,\mathbb D\mathscr F).
\tag{VSD11.3}
\] Its first arrow is \[
G\longmapsto\left([a]\longmapsto
\sum_\rho\operatorname{Res}_{s=\rho}
\frac{\tfrac12\mathcal M_0a(s)G(1-s)}{\zeta(s)}\,ds\right).
\tag{VSD11.4}
\] The denominator is the original zeta, and the residues and ideal
retain all zero multiplicities. The comparison does not replace it by
the source transform \[
F_0(s)=\frac{s(s-1)}8\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s).
\tag{VSD11.5}
\] All of that transform's factors, endpoint values, trivial-zero
derivatives and local-unit derivatives remain those proved in RD8 and
CDI12. The four endpoint lines are explicitly retained in
\(E_+^*\oplus E_-^*\) and \(E_+'\oplus E_-'\). Their dagger quotient
vanishes because they are finite dimensional, not because their original
contributions were deleted.

Every continuous coefficient operator preserves \(E'\subset E^*\) under
ordinary transposition and thus induces an operator on \(E^\dagger\).
Gysin is coefficient-natural. Thus the entire comparison triangle
intertwines the already proved coefficient, cover and mirror maps,
retaining their signs and factors. This does not choose a new arithmetic
degree convention; the cover/trace derivation is a separate calculation.
Ordinary transpose, inverse-parameter contragredient, and residue
degree-character comparison remain the distinct maps proved in
CDI6--CDI10.

\section{VSD12. Actual output for the support-dual
calculation}\label{vsd12.-actual-output-for-the-support-dual-calculation}

The actual \(\mathscr F\) now has an explicit ordinary algebraic Verdier
dual, including both pole Gysin maps, positive orientation, the minus on
dualized restrictions, every stalk and costalk, and full global
cohomology. These proofs apply to the actual infinite coefficient spaces
without a finite-rank duality assumption.

The continuous-dual coefficient complexes have an actual sheaf receiver
\(\mathscr D_c\mathscr F\) and a proved map to ordinary Verdier duality.
Its cone is the specific object in VSD8, with every coefficient group
and support map computed. Its nonzero difference is retained and studied
in VSD9--VSD10. This supplies the exact comparison required before using
either category in the support-duality part of a Deligne-style argument.

No finite-rank étale realization, Deligne weight bound, arithmetic
purity, or RH conclusion is an assumption or conclusion here. The
subsequent weight calculation can use the proved cone and
coefficient-category maps instead of a presumed equality of the two
duals.

\section{VSD13. The exact comparison defect admits every rational
operation in the Mellin multiplication
operator}\label{vsd13.-the-exact-comparison-defect-admits-every-rational-operation-in-the-mellin-multiplication-operator}

The nonzero comparison object has additional algebraic structure which
can be calculated globally. Let \[
\mathcal B=\left\{F\text{ entire}:
\sup_{|\Re s|\le R}(1+|\Im s|)^M|F(s)|<\infty
\text{ for all }R,M\in\mathbb N\right\},
\quad
\mathcal I=\Theta J,\quad\mathcal Q=\mathcal B/\mathcal I,
\] \[
L:\mathcal B\to\mathcal B,\qquad (LF)(s)=sF(s).
\tag{VSD13.1}
\] The topological isomorphism \(\Theta:A\to\mathcal B\) and its
restriction \(J\to\mathcal I\) are the actual Mellin comparison of CDI6
and SSI, retaining \(\Theta=\tfrac12\mathcal M_0\). The operator \(L\)
is continuous, preserves \(\mathcal I\), and induces an operator on
\(\mathcal Q\). These are the domains and maps being transposed below.

For every \(\mu\in\mathbb C\), multiplication \[
M_\mu=L-\mu:\mathcal B\longrightarrow\mathcal B
\tag{VSD13.2}
\] is injective and has image exactly the closed hyperplane
\(F(\mu)=0\). Its inverse on that image is division by \(s-\mu\). That
inverse is continuous: outside the disk \(|s-\mu|<1\), the quotient is
bounded by the original function; inside, the maximum principle applied
to the holomorphic quotient bounds it using a circle of radius two
centered at \(\mu\). Every coefficient seminorm on that circle is
bounded by one of the larger-strip seminorms on \(\mathcal B\), and the
polynomial imaginary-coordinate weight is bounded on the disk. This
gives a finite seminorm bound for each target seminorm. Evaluation onto
\(\mathbb C\) is surjective, since \(e^{(s-\mu)^2}\in\mathcal B\) has
value one at \(\mu\). Thus the image really has codimension one.

The same multiplication on \(\mathcal I\) is injective with closed
codimension-one image. To prove this at every \(\mu\), retain the
complete function \[
F_0(s)=\frac{s(s-1)}8\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)\in\mathcal I.
\tag{VSD13.3}
\] Its zero divisor is the complete actual nontrivial-zero divisor, with
all multiplicities, as retained in RD1 and RD8. Every \(F\in\mathcal I\)
therefore has an entire quotient \(F/F_0\); no claim that this quotient
belongs to \(\mathcal B\) is needed. Define \[
\ell_\mu(F)=
\begin{cases}
F(\mu)/F_0(\mu),&F_0(\mu)\ne0,\\
F^{(m)}(\mu)/F_0^{(m)}(\mu),&
F_0\text{ has a zero of order }m\text{ at }\mu .
\end{cases}
\tag{VSD13.4}
\] This is the precise removable value \((F/F_0)(\mu)\). Cauchy's
estimate makes it continuous; the nonzero denominator derivative is
retained. Since \(\ell_\mu(F_0)=1\), it is onto. The image of
\(M_\mu:\mathcal I\to\mathcal I\) is exactly \(\ker\ell_\mu\). Necessity
follows by taking the quotient by \(F_0\). Conversely, when
\(\ell_\mu(F)=0\), division by \(s-\mu\) leaves the full required order
of vanishing at \(\mu\) and preserves every other required zero jet, so
the quotient belongs to \(\mathcal I\). Its continuity follows from the
division estimate just proved in \(\mathcal B\), restricted to these
closed subspaces. This proves the entire statement, including at every
multiple zero and at each endpoint or trivial-zero location where
\(F_0\) is nonzero.

Here is the general transpose calculation applied to these two actual
operators. Suppose \(M:E\to E\) is a continuous injective map onto a
closed subspace of finite codimension, with continuous inverse on that
image. Its algebraic transpose \(M^*:E^*\to E^*\) is onto, by
algebraically extending the functional \(Mx\mapsto\lambda(x)\) from the
image. Its continuous transpose \(M':E'\to E'\) is onto as well: the
same functional is continuous on the image when \(\lambda\) is
continuous, and Hahn--Banach extends it to \(E\). Moreover \[
\ker M^*=\ker M'
\tag{VSD13.5}
\] as subspaces of \(E^*\). Both are all functionals on the
finite-dimensional Hausdorff quotient \(E/M(E)\), and every such
functional is continuous. Consequently \[
M^\dagger:E^\dagger\longrightarrow E^\dagger
\tag{VSD13.6}
\] is bijective. Surjectivity follows from surjectivity of \(M^*\). For
injectivity, if \(M^*\lambda\) is continuous, choose a continuous
\(\nu\) with \(M'\nu=M^*\lambda\); then
\(\lambda-\nu\in\ker M^*=\ker M'\), so \(\lambda\) itself is continuous.

Applying this proved calculation to (VSD13.2) and to its restriction to
\(\mathcal I\) yields \[
L^\dagger-\mu:\mathcal B^\dagger\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal B^\dagger,
\qquad
L^\dagger-\mu:\mathcal I^\dagger\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal I^\dagger
\quad(\mu\in\mathbb C).
\tag{VSD13.7}
\] Here \(L^\dagger\) means the operator induced by the ordinary
transpose \(L^*\) on the indicated dual quotient. It is not
multiplication on the original primal space.

The exact dual-quotient row \[
0\to\mathcal Q^\dagger\to\mathcal B^\dagger\to\mathcal I^\dagger\to0
\tag{VSD13.8}
\] commutes with these operators. It follows, by a direct diagram chase,
that \[
\boxed{L^\dagger-\mu:
\mathcal Q^\dagger\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal Q^\dagger
\quad\text{for every }\mu\in\mathbb C.}
\tag{VSD13.9}
\] Injectivity follows from the middle bijection. For surjectivity,
solve the equation in \(\mathcal B^\dagger\); the image of its solution
in \(\mathcal I^\dagger\) is killed by \(L^\dagger-\mu\), so it is zero
by (VSD13.7). The solution therefore lies in the injected
\(\mathcal Q^\dagger\). Transport through \(\Theta\) gives the same
statements on \(A^\dagger,J^\dagger,Q^\dagger\), and through the
explicit endpoint splittings on \(V_p^\dagger,Z^\dagger\).

Every nonzero polynomial \(P\) over \(\mathbb C\) factors into a nonzero
scalar times linear factors. Thus \(P(L^\dagger)\) is bijective on all
these defect coefficients. The usual commuting inverses define a unique
extension of their \(\mathbb C[t]\)-module structure to a vector-space
structure over the rational-function field \(\mathbb C(t)\): \[
\frac{P(t)}{Q(t)}\cdot x
=P(L^\dagger)\,Q(L^\dagger)^{-1}x,\qquad Q\ne0.
\tag{VSD13.10}
\] This is independent of the fractional presentation because cross
multiplication gives identical commuting operators. Every map in the
dagger coefficient diagram commutes with \(L^\dagger\) and hence with
these inverses. Consequently the entire comparison object (VSD8.2),
including its Gysin maps, can be formed on these
\(\mathbb C(t)\)-coefficient spaces.

In particular none of these coefficients has a nonzero generalized
\(L^\dagger\)-eigenvector of any finite order: \((L^\dagger-\mu)^m x=0\)
implies \(x=0\). The actual finite zero-jet residue vectors are in the
continuous subobject, and their image in the dagger quotient is zero.
This proves a global property of the precise extra coefficient sector
rather than stopping at its nonzero existence.

One distinction is essential. On a discontinuous algebraic functional,
one cannot move that functional through a limit merely because the
original coefficient action is differentiable. The \(L^\dagger\) above
is the induced transpose of the explicitly defined operator (VSD13.1).
This proof does not identify it with differentiation of the algebraic
action \(T_a^*\) on arbitrary discontinuous functionals. Therefore the
absence of generalized \(L^\dagger\)-eigenvectors by itself does not
classify all characters of that algebraic dilation action, does not
prove a weight bound, and does not erase the comparison sector. It gives
the exact rational-operator structure with the domains, maps and
limitation of the inference specified.

There is an exact finite-sector comparison in both kernel and cokernel.
For \(E=A,J,Q\) with these transported operators, and every nonzero
polynomial \(P\), inclusion \(E'\hookrightarrow E^*\) induces \[
\boxed{
\ker P(L')\xrightarrow{\sim}\ker P(L^*),\qquad
\operatorname{coker}P(L')\xrightarrow{\sim}
\operatorname{coker}P(L^*).}
\tag{VSD13.11}
\] These are algebraic kernel and cokernel identifications with their
actual maps; no topological quotient assertion is inserted. For the
kernel, a functional killed by \(P(L^*)\) has dagger class killed by the
bijection \(P(L^\dagger)\), so it is continuous. For surjectivity of the
cokernel map, given \(\lambda\in E^*\), solve
\(P(L^\dagger)\bar\mu=\bar\lambda\), lift \(\bar\mu\) to \(\mu\in E^*\),
and observe \(\lambda-P(L^*)\mu\in E'\). For injectivity, if continuous
\(\eta\) equals \(P(L^*)\lambda\), bijectivity on the dagger quotient
forces \(\lambda\in E'\).

Every finite-dimensional \(L^*\)-invariant subspace \(M\subset E^*\) is
consequently contained in \(E'\). Its finite-dimensional operator has a
nonzero characteristic polynomial \(P\) annihilating \(M\); the adjugate
identity for \(tI-L^*|_M\), evaluated at that operator, proves the
assertion. Therefore \[
\boxed{M\subset\ker P(L^*)=\ker P(L')\subset E'.}
\tag{VSD13.12}
\] For every \(\mu\) and \(m\ge1\), the entire kernels of
\((L^*-\mu)^m\) and \((L'-\mu)^m\) agree, with no dimension bound needed
for that kernel equality. Thus the two categories have identical full
polynomial kernels and cokernels through their stated inclusion.

Replacing \(L\) by \(L+k\), for any stated scalar \(k\), preserves this
result because \(P(t+k)\) is a nonzero polynomial. The retained
normal-degree shift therefore leaves the finite-sector comparison valid.
On \(Z\) and \(V_p\), retain their actual continuous endpoint blocks
separately; all functionals on those finite blocks are continuous, and
the explicit splitting reduces the other block to the \(J\) calculation.
This extends (VSD13.11)--(VSD13.12) to those specified operators without
dropping endpoints.

These consequences concern the explicit multiplication operator. They do
not assume differentiation of discontinuous dual functionals or classify
arbitrary dilation characters. They supply the exact finite-sector
comparison from the calculated defect.

\section{VSD14. Independent check of the completed trace

Here is a direct verification of the new action on that completion. Put
\[

The complete residue isomorphism

\section{CV0. Exact inputs and scope}\label{cv0.-exact-inputs-and-scope}

The supporting datum remains
\(\tau\langle Z_1;\mathrm{no}\ Z_2\rangle\). This calculation acts on
the already reconstructed coefficient spaces and the sphere receiver; it
puts no coordinate, metric, addition or scalar operation on \(\tau\).
The source stage, full-history requirement, retracted addition and

The accepted CC\_CONTINUOUS\_SUPPORT\_DUAL\_SHEAF.md, CSD0--CSD12, is

The source identity and original-author reading coverage remain CSD0 and

complete human papers.

Write \(E'\) for continuous complex-linear functionals,
\(E^*=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(E,\mathbb C)\) for all algebraic
functionals, and \(E^\dagger=E^*/E'\) as a vector space. No topology is
imposed on a discontinuous functional or on this quotient. The objective
is a literal morphism of sheaf complexes, and then a verification of
